nodes.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
nodes.title: The contract identity

nodes.prose:
Every controller and compiler-helper envelope carries these string fields
under `build`. They identify the emitting binary's compiled context.
nodes.title: Build identification

nodes.prose:
The Git HEAD object name observed by the packaged build, or `unknown` when
unavailable. Direct Rust compilation reads `PW_BUILD_COMMIT` with an absent
value falling back to `unknown`. Describe and commit report provenance;
identity admission compares the contract field.
nodes.title: Commit

nodes.prose:
The public identity embedded in the emitting binary. Receiving boundaries use
the exact value according to their identity-admission rule.
nodes.title: Contract

nodes.prose:
The descriptive source coordinate compiled into the producer. `build.sh`
uses `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty`, falling back
to `unknown`. Direct Rust compilation reads `PW_BUILD_DESCRIBE` with an absent
value falling back to `unknown`.
nodes.title: Describe

nodes.prose:
The build-number string. `build.sh` uses nonempty `PW_BUILD_NUMBER` when
supplied, otherwise the Git commit count, falling back to `0`. Direct Rust
compilation reads `PW_BUILD_NUMBER`, falling back to `unknown` when absent.
nodes.title: Number

nodes.prose:
The packaged build's version string. `build.sh` uses nonempty `PW_VERSION`
when supplied; otherwise it takes the leading three-part version from its
Git describe value, falling back to `0.0.0`. Direct Rust compilation reads
`PW_BUILD_VERSION`, falling back to `unknown` when absent.
nodes.title: Version

nodes.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
nodes.title: Absent field

nodes.prose:
An actor names a declared worker role, sandbox setup and its visits to the
schedule. Actor identity is the request's identifier and associated owned
process evidence. A numeric PID records one observation of that association.
nodes.title: Actor

nodes.prose:
An assessment is a conclusion computed from named observations and declared
relations, such as query order, operation/target relation, application state
or process disposition. Its applicability and supporting observations belong
to that assessment. Raw observation retention and permission to use an
assessment are separately reported consequences of a failed check.
nodes.title: Assessment

nodes.prose:
A byte field identifies its byte source, encoding, total/retained length and
bound where applicable. Hexadecimal and base64 are representations of bytes;
decoded diagnostic text is a separate projection. UTF-8 byte counts and
character counts use the units named by each capacity.
nodes.title: Byte observation

nodes.prose:
A client capture records reservation attempts, invocation knowledge, transport
results and host reply bytes as observed by the client. A received host frame
inside an admitted capture has its own producer admission.
nodes.title: Capture

nodes.prose:
A cause identifies why an event occurred. Permission-shaped return values
support the `permission_failure` observation class; they leave sandbox cause
unresolved. A termination request and a later owned reap support the specific
lifecycle relationship stated by the lifecycle assessment. Query answers and
attempt returns retain their individual observation scopes.
nodes.title: Cause

nodes.prose:
The runner client acquires a reservation, submits the held request over XPC
and returns a typed capture of its transport observations and received host
bytes. The controller invokes it once for a run.
nodes.title: Runner client

nodes.prose:
A closed input object accepts its listed keys; an unknown key is refused at
the boundary enforcing that object. Map keys, such as policy parameter names,
are values in their declared domain and have their own constraints.
nodes.title: Closed object

nodes.prose:
A closed vocabulary admits the specified set of values. The rule names the
component and boundary that identifies another value as invalid, and states
the consequence for retained records and supported assessments.
nodes.title: Closed value vocabulary

nodes.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
nodes.title: Controller

nodes.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
nodes.title: Effect

nodes.prose:
An envelope is the outer JSON record emitted by the controller or compiler
helper: `kind`, generation time, build identification, result and data. Its
result describes the emitting operation; contained query, attempt and child
results retain their own meanings.
nodes.title: Envelope

nodes.prose:
`sbpl-check` reads policy input, inventories imports and calls the native
compiler. Its compiler result is reported in its own envelope. The standalone
helper and the controller's fallback invocation have separately stated input
and invocation conditions.
nodes.title: Compiler helper

nodes.prose:
The XPC host admits the request, prepares worker resources, coordinates query
collection and action release, collects worker/validator observations and
produces the host reply. Specimen policy application occurs in the worker so
the host retains its reply path.
nodes.title: Runner host

nodes.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
nodes.title: Null value

nodes.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
nodes.title: Observation

nodes.prose:
An open vocabulary admits values beyond the displayed list. Its field
definition states how unfamiliar values are retained or classified. Whether
the displayed list is exhaustive is recorded separately from admission.
nodes.title: Open value vocabulary

nodes.prose:
An optional field permits the absence specified by its record definition.
Conditional presence, explicit null and omitted serialization each retain
their own stated conditions.
nodes.title: Optional field

nodes.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
nodes.title: Phase

nodes.prose:
PolicyWitness, abbreviated PW, is the controller, runner client, runner host,
native worker, query validator and compiler helper distributed together. The
controller exposes specimen execution, runner management and version reporting.
nodes.title: PolicyWitness

nodes.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
nodes.title: Prediction

nodes.prose:
A probe pairs a declared sandbox query with a declared native attempt and
assigns them a step ID. Query operation/filter and attempt kind/action/target
are separate submitted operands, whose relationships the comparison records.
nodes.title: Probe

nodes.prose:
A host reply is the host-produced execution record, including its producer
identity, execution summary and available observations. The typed host frame
carries this record across XPC. Raw retained bytes and an admitted decoded
reply have different availability and interpretation conditions.
nodes.title: Reply

nodes.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
nodes.title: Request

nodes.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
nodes.title: Specimen

nodes.prose:
Unknown means the available record leaves a factual question unresolved.
Missing process status, absent completed result and unavailable provenance
therefore preserve the corresponding uncertainty. An explicit observation of
absence, such as an owned service confirmed absent, has its own evidence.
nodes.title: Unknown fact

nodes.prose:
The native `sb_api_validator` issues `sandbox_check` queries about the selected
worker process and returns query records to the host. Each query describes
an operation and filter; the attempt later performs its separately specified
native operation.
nodes.title: Validator

nodes.prose:
The native worker receives policy input and its own action plan, applies the
declared sandbox when requested, executes released actions and publishes
bounded observations in host-provided regions. The ordinary form uses one
fresh worker; the actor form assigns a fresh worker to each actor it launches.
nodes.title: Worker

nodes.prose:
Fixed byte length of the CodeDirectory hashes admitted from equipment
inventory and code inspection.
nodes.title: CodeDirectory hash byte width

nodes.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
nodes.title: CodeDirectory hexadecimal width

nodes.prose:
Fixed byte length of SHA-256 digests used for the schema fingerprint, worker
identity and signed-file hashes.
nodes.title: SHA-256 digest length

nodes.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
nodes.title: SHA-256 hexadecimal width

nodes.prose:
The typed response frame carries a SHA-256 fingerprint of its wire schema.
Its selected schema representation includes record IDs/names, field tags,
names and encoded types, optional and null representation, projections,
variants and roots. The receiver checks this fingerprint before decoding the
producer context for public identity admission. A matching fingerprint
establishes the selected wire-schema match; the public producer identity is
then checked separately.
nodes.title: Wire-schema fingerprint

nodes.prose:
The host/worker protocol identity is a SHA-256 digest, carried as raw bytes or
lowercase hexadecimal using the fixed widths below. It covers sorted C/header/Swift inputs
under `controller/tools/pw_probe_runner` and `runner/Sources`, together with
`docs/generate_worker_identity.py`, `docs/source_identity.py`, `build.sh`,
`meson.build`, `meson.options` and `runner/Package.swift`. Its domain prefix is
`PolicyWitness host/worker source identity` followed by NUL; path and contents
use the same unsigned eight-byte big-endian length framing. Generated identity
region bodies are excluded while their boundary markers remain inputs.

The worker compares its embedded value and bootstrap magic with the host's
shared header before reading the remaining protocol state. A mapping failure
returns worker exit 3; a mapped header mismatch returns exit 4. Host decoding
of `worker_evidence` also requires a matching header. A reported `abi_identity` identifies
the protocol sources selected by the host; establishing the executing binary's
association uses the equipment and launch evidence.
nodes.title: Worker protocol identity

nodes.prose:
The host's typed reply carries this producer record. Each field comes from the
host's compiled build context.
nodes.title: Host producer identification

nodes.prose:
The host build's observed Git HEAD object name, or `unknown` when the compiled
context has no such observation. Identity admission uses `contract`; this field
retains the host's provenance.
nodes.title: Commit

nodes.prose:
The host's public identity, independently compared by a receiver before the
reply's execution records supply interpretations.
nodes.title: Contract

nodes.prose:
The host build's descriptive Git coordinate, or `unknown` in the ordinary
unbound Swift build context. Packaged context generation supplies the observed
build description.
nodes.title: Describe

nodes.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.
nodes.title: Exact admission identity

facts.free.effect: Derive the public identity from the selected source tree, embed it in compiled producers and property lists, and refuse signing if recomputation after compilation yields a different identity.

nodes.prose:
The packaged build computes the identity itself and passes that value into
its Rust and Swift producers. Swift context generation recomputes it and
refuses a supplied `PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` that differs. The pre-sign comparison
refuses a selected-source change during compilation.
nodes.title: Build derivation

nodes.prose:
The Rust controller and compiler helper embed a nonempty compile-time
`PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` verbatim. An absent or empty value becomes `unbound`.
Ordinary SwiftPM compilation uses `unbound`; its explicitly selected unit-test
context uses `test:policy-witness`. Rust unit tests likewise use
`test:policy-witness`. A request cannot pass the controller's identity gate
when its expected identity is empty or `unbound`.
nodes.title: Direct compilation contexts

nodes.prose:
The direct Rust environment path is established by the compile-time constant
and Cargo's environment tracking. The available plain-Cargo integration check
removes `PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` and establishes the unbound case. A direct Cargo
build with an explicitly supplied foreign or release-form identity has not
been exercised in this examination.
nodes.title: Direct-build evidence limit

nodes.prose:
`release:vX.Y.Z` names the sole annotated release tag at the build checkout's
HEAD. The build derives this form when the checkout is clean, the tag matches
`v<digits>.<digits>.<digits>`, and the selected files' actual bytes and inventory
equal that tag's blobs. More than one qualifying annotated tag on a clean
HEAD refuses identity derivation as ambiguous.

`development:<sha256>` identifies the selected source paths and bytes in
other source trees. Its digest is SHA-256 with the domain prefix
`PolicyWitness public build contract` followed by a NUL byte. For each sorted
repository-relative path, the generator appends the UTF-8 path and file bytes,
each preceded by its unsigned eight-byte big-endian length. A dirty release
checkout receives this development form. A documentation-only edit can change
the form from release to development while leaving the selected-source digest
unchanged.
nodes.title: Release and development forms

nodes.prose:
The development digest includes `.rs`, `.c`, `.h`, `.swift`, `.sb`, `.plist`
and `.ent` files discovered under `controller/src`, `controller/tools`,
`runner/Sources`, `runner/Clients`, `runner/Services` and `runner/augments`.
It also includes `build.sh`, `meson.build`, `meson.options`,
`runner/Package.swift`, `controller/Cargo.toml`, `controller/Cargo.lock`,
`controller/build.rs`, `Info.plist`, `PolicyWitness.entitlements`,
`docs/build_contract.py`, `docs/source_identity.py`,
`tests/build_equipment.py`, `tests/build-evidence.py`, and the build helpers
`tests/lib/build_provenance.py`, `signer_check.py`, `cargo_config.py`,
`checkout_lock.py` and `output_target.py` in that same directory.

Discovery uses the same inventory in a checkout and a source copy. Missing
declared inputs, symlinks under the selected roots and nonregular source
objects refuse derivation. The digest's equality concerns those paths and
bytes; build configuration, signing identity, SDK and observed runtime
behavior are recorded and checked by their respective operations.
nodes.title: Selected build inputs

facts.free.effect: Walk reachable annotated release tags in ancestry order, retain each surface's last changed stamp and removal state, and mark changed current inputs unreleased or with the explicitly prepared release.

nodes.prose:
History derivation compares a surface with its prior declared inputs. The
history reader for a released layout supplies that layout's own definition
and shape framing. Source copies lacking annotated history can check current
inputs and agreement of carried tables; their result explicitly leaves the
historical last-change derivation unverified.
nodes.title: Deriving the history table

nodes.prose:
A development identity names a source digest, while the table is indexed by
releases. The current reuse procedure leaves the comparison baseline for a
development-asserting specimen unspecified. Exact admission still uses the
target identity; the development-to-release review workflow needs a stated
baseline or an explicit review of the relevant target definitions.
nodes.title: Development specimen review

nodes.prose:
An ordinary build accepts the narrower source-copy check. Requiring complete
release history for that build would change which source distributions can
build; the requirement remains a maintainer decision. Strict release
preflight requires complete history.
nodes.title: Ordinary-build history requirement

nodes.prose:
Ordinary checks without annotated history verify current authored content,
canonical shapes, the public snapshot and agreement of both carried stamp
tables. They report the historical last-change derivation as unverified.
Ordinary regeneration and explicit release preparation require every release
claimed by the carried tables and public snapshot; missing history refuses
before writing generated outputs. Released snapshots retain their historical
dependencies even when every surface has since changed.
nodes.title: Source copies and release preparation

nodes.prose:
A surface groups a named part of the public contract and its canonical shape
inputs. Its stamp records the last reachable annotated release at which those
declared inputs changed. A pending change is `unreleased` until a release is
prepared. A removed surface retains a removal row. The table directs review
to changed definitions; admission uses the exact public identity carried by
the request or record.

An unchanged stamp establishes equality of the inputs used by that stamp
derivation. A changed implementation can require review even when its prose
and shape inputs have remained unchanged. Reasserting a saved specimen for a
different build remains an explicit choice about the target's commitments.
nodes.title: Surface and stamp

nodes.prose:
Current dispatch selects version reporting from the first argument and ignores
remaining arguments. The intended argument-count commitment is unresolved;
the source establishes this acceptance, while the version check exercises the
single-argument form.
nodes.title: Trailing version arguments

nodes.prose:
The controller's public identity, also carried in the same envelope's
`build.contract`.
nodes.title: Reported identity

facts.free.condition: The first command argument is --version or version.
facts.free.effect: Emit a kind version envelope with result.ok true, result.exit_code 0, other result fields null and the current build context; return process exit 0 after successful rendering, or 2 when envelope rendering returns an error.

nodes.prose:
Version dispatch reports the compiled context without loading a specimen or
starting the runner client. `generated_at_unix_ms` is the producer's current
wall-clock time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; the shared serializer
uses zero if its system time precedes that epoch.
nodes.title: Version command

nodes.prose: A saved specimen describes one experiment. The controller reads its file once, resolves controller options and packaged augments, and serializes the held request delivered to the client. Direct XPC callers supply the host form themselves. The standalone compiler helper accepts its own policy input.
nodes.title: Saved specimens and runner selection

nodes.prose: These fields extend the saved-file root at the controller entry. The controller strips all five before client delivery. A direct XPC request carrying them reaches the host unknown-field refusal.
nodes.title: Controller selection options

facts.free.effect: Retain a target-resolution error while resolving augment dossiers. If target resolution failed, report tool_error and exit 2; otherwise an augment refusal reports bad_request and exit 1. Neither branch invokes the client.

Validate every supplied legacy value first, then let each non-null nested value replace its corresponding legacy value. An explicit nested empty entitlement list replaces the legacy list. Refuse standard mode with an external selector and byoxpc mode without an ID or service.

nodes.prose: CLI `--runner-mode` is parsed before reading the request and is injected into its selector processing. `machme` is refused. Selection resolution and entitlement checks precede client invocation. A resolved target identifies the requested host service; actor equipment roles remain actor declarations.
nodes.title: Selector precedence

nodes.prose: Legacy list of selected-worker entitlement keys required to be boolean true. Null means absent. Values must be strings.
nodes.title: required_entitlements

nodes.prose: Optional nested selector object. Null means absent. Unknown nested keys are refused.
nodes.title: runner

nodes.prose: Legacy registry ID selector. Null means absent; a non-string value refuses even when nested `runner.id` would override it.
nodes.title: runner_id

nodes.prose: Legacy runner mode. Null means absent. The accepted values are `standard` and `byoxpc`.
nodes.title: runner_mode

nodes.prose: Legacy explicit Mach service selector. Null means absent; a non-string value refuses before nested precedence is applied.
nodes.title: runner_service

nodes.prose: These controls are admitted as request data in the current implementation, including packaged hosts. Their names identify test use; the parser applies the documented grammar and capacities.
nodes.title: Execution overrides

nodes.prose: Actor equipment role-to-path map. Present maps must be nonempty and use only `selected` and `unentitled` keys; actor admission requires absolute paths. The ordinary form refuses this map.
nodes.title: actor_equipment_executable_paths

nodes.prose: A caller whose connection passes host authorization can supply these controls. Actor equipment preparation checks the packaged inventory and both packaged role bindings before considering fixture override bindings. It retains the packaged and test_override rows with their respective implementation identities.
nodes.title: Override admission and equipment ordering

nodes.prose: The draft has inspected the decoder and timeout planning. Existing signed-app cases exercise several overrides; a complete mapping of overrides to boundary assertions and applicable release results remains to be assembled, including downstream worker-argument refusal for excessive values. This gap records incomplete evidence attribution across the override set.
nodes.title: Override fixture coverage

nodes.prose: The signal-number bound 31 remains a source-owned grammar value. Collection floors are selected by the production planning helpers and checked against the limits inventory. The ordinary worker floor and fixture-delay caps have controls calling the production planning helper and argument parser. Actor admission currently accepts worker_timeout_ms although actor execution uses its fixed allowance. Whether to refuse that inapplicable override remains an admission decision.
nodes.title: Override quantities and applicability

nodes.prose: Validator executable override, bounded by <!-- span limits.test_override_path.value_unit -->1,023 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. The validator remains a separate child and receives query work through its own channel.
nodes.title: validator_executable_path

nodes.prose: Per-validator I/O timeout override in milliseconds. The host floors the proposed allowance at <!-- span limits.validator_io_override_floor.value_unit -->50 milliseconds<!-- /span -->; omission uses <!-- span limits.validator_io_wait.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The remaining aggregate collection allowance can reduce the effective timeout below that floor.
nodes.title: validator_io_timeout_ms

nodes.prose: Cumulative validator collection budget override in milliseconds, spanning phases. Both schedulers clamp it to a minimum of <!-- span limits.validator_collection_override_floor.value_unit -->1 millisecond<!-- /span --> and their configured maximum: <!-- span limits.phase_collection_wait.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> for the ordinary form and <!-- span limits.actor_collection_allowance.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> for actors. Omission uses that maximum.
nodes.title: validator_total_timeout_ms

nodes.prose: Ordinary-worker executable override, bounded by <!-- span limits.test_override_path.value_unit -->1,023 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. Actor-form admission refuses this singular override.
nodes.title: worker_executable_path

nodes.prose: Nonnegative zero-based slot in each worker's own plan. After that attempt returns and its result payload is written, the worker raises SIGKILL before publishing completion. Negative values are omitted. The worker argument parser requires an index below <!-- span limits.probe_steps.value_unit -->256 items<!-- /span -->; an index beyond the worker's actual plan has no reached action to trigger it.
nodes.title: worker_kill_before_publish_slot

nodes.prose: Positive fixture delay in milliseconds after all declared visits and actions, before terminal publication. The host forwards positive values; the worker argument parser accepts through <!-- span limits.worker_fixture_delay.value_unit -->60,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. A larger forwarded value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted by the host.
nodes.title: worker_post_apply_hang_ms

nodes.prose: Positive fixture signal requested after completed actions and before terminal publication, including an unapplied actor's visits. The host forwards positive values; the worker accepts signal numbers through 31. A larger value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted. A signal request can return without termination; final process observations decide the ending.
nodes.title: worker_post_apply_kill_signal

nodes.prose: Positive fixture delay in milliseconds after compilation and optional capture, before an apply worker's readiness byte and policy application. The host forwards positive values; the worker argument parser accepts through <!-- span limits.worker_fixture_delay.value_unit -->60,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. A larger value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted. The unapplied actor branch bypasses this compile/readiness path.
nodes.title: worker_pre_ready_hang_ms

nodes.prose: Ordinary worker sentinel budget override in milliseconds. The host floors the supplied allowance at <!-- span limits.worker_timeout_override_floor.value_unit -->50 milliseconds<!-- /span -->; omission uses <!-- span limits.worker_sentinel_wait.value_unit -->120,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. Actor scheduling uses its fixed <!-- span limits.actor_execution_allowance.value_unit -->120,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> allowance even when this field is supplied.
nodes.title: worker_timeout_ms

nodes.prose: A nested field overrides a valid legacy value only when non-null.
nodes.title: Nested runner selector

nodes.prose: Registry ID for an installed external runner.
nodes.title: id

nodes.prose: Mode constraint applied to selection. With no mode or external selector, selection uses the packaged standard runner.
nodes.title: mode

nodes.prose: Selected-worker entitlement keys that must read back as boolean true for selection. This demand is separate from each actor's required_entitlements.
nodes.title: required_entitlements

nodes.prose: Explicit external Mach service name.
nodes.title: service

nodes.prose: The host request objects have closed field sets. Parameter-map keys and caller labels are data within their own bounds.
nodes.title: Specimen

nodes.prose: Optional execution controls accepted by the host request decoder. Each declared control retains its stated scope and meaning; unknown override fields are refused.
nodes.title: _test_overrides

nodes.prose: A non-null actor array selects the actor form; an empty array is refused. Each declared actor has its own fresh worker and at least one declared visit. Omission or null selects the ordinary form.
nodes.title: actors

facts.free.effect: Check contract first, decode the selected plan form and closed nested objects, check capacities, then validate policy and plan meaning. A refusal returns bad_request with no worker or validator execution and an empty steps array. A host may already exist to deliver this refusal.

nodes.prose: The decoder follows its object and branch order. A capacity failure can precede a semantic failure in a successfully decoded object. Admission accepts or refuses the complete plan; it preserves declared action counts. Empty ordinary plans still compile and apply the policy.
nodes.title: Admission order and effects

nodes.prose:
This template applies a policy with no probe actions. Replace the assertion with the packaged version's `build.contract` before submission.

```json
{"contract":"<reported-contract>","specimen_id":"apply-only","policy":{"format":"sbpl","sbpl_source":"(version 1) (allow default)"},"probe_plan":[]}
```
nodes.title: Apply-only specimen

facts.free.effect: Refuse excess before launch: <!-- span limits.policy_source.value_unit -->262,143 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> per final policy source, <!-- span limits.probe_steps.value_unit -->256 items<!-- /span --> total actions, <!-- span limits.phase_count.value_unit -->8 items<!-- /span --> ordinary phases, and <!-- span limits.actor_phases.value_unit -->16 items<!-- /span --> actor phases. Preserve complete UTF-8 strings at accepted bounds.

nodes.prose: Native C-string inputs also refuse embedded NUL. Host-only labels use their declared UTF-8 capacities. Unicode is counted by encoded bytes. A paired query and attempt consumes one action; an extension action consumes one action and contributes no query. Phase and actor counts do not multiply the total action capacity.
nodes.title: Bounded strings and action counts

nodes.prose: Required non-null string asserting the exact public contract identity. The controller checks it before selector parsing and augmentation; the host checks it before other request fields. Obtain the current value from the packaged version envelope. `unbound` is refused.
nodes.title: contract

nodes.prose: The exact handling of repeated JSON object keys across the controller parser and Swift decoder still requires a paired boundary control. The closed-field and branch-order obligations above concern the object each decoder produces.
nodes.title: Duplicate-key decoding

facts.free.effect: Read and parse the request file once; gate its contract, parse selection, resolve named augments, strip controller selector fields and serialize once for client delivery. Preserve original and selected policy observations in the specimen dossier.

nodes.title: Hold and deliver the selected request

facts.free.effect: Treat optional null as absent where decodeIfPresent is used. Refuse present null for actor equipment, actor required_entitlements, after_termination and actor_equipment_executable_paths. Retain presence of extension operands so an inapplicable operand is refused even when null.

nodes.prose: Ordered phase declarations. The ordinary form requires a nonempty array, forbids actor ownership, termination dependencies and extension actions, and uses one worker across its phases. The actor form requires phases and forbids a non-null `probe_plan`.
nodes.title: phases

nodes.prose: Policy for the ordinary form. With no non-null `actors`, the policy object is required. In the actor form a non-null top-level policy is refused; each actor declares its own sandbox mode and policy.
nodes.title: policy

nodes.prose: Ordinary paired probes, including an empty array for apply-only execution. Exactly one of this field and `phases` must be non-null in the ordinary form. The host represents this plan as the `main` phase.
nodes.title: probe_plan

nodes.prose: Optional caller label, bounded by <!-- span limits.request_label.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. Omission and null have the same meaning; it selects no execution mode.
nodes.title: run_kind

nodes.prose: Required non-null string caller label, echoed when it fits <!-- span limits.specimen_id.value_unit -->255 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. It may be empty. Its identity is independent of the worker PID or an actor ID.
nodes.title: specimen_id

accounting govern satisfaction. These are charged-wait conditions; operating
system scheduling determines when the host next runs.

shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.
shared.title: Associating the owned process

shared.prose:
| Operation | Required operands | Producing actor and consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue` | `family`, `target`, `authority`, `token_ref` | Active actor calls native file issuance once with class selected by authority, exact target and flags zero; assigns the declared token resource. |
| `transfer` | `token_ref`, `recipient`, `delivery_ref` | Token-owning actor publishes a host request for one assigned recipient slot; assigns the delivery resource. |
| `consume` | `delivery_ref`, `handle_ref` | Recipient actor calls native consume on its usable delivered token; assigns the handle resource. |
| `release` | `handle_ref` | Consuming actor calls native release for its candidate handle. |

Each other operand must be absent. A required null operand is missing for this grammar; an extraneous null operand is inapplicable.

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
shared.title: Absent field

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
shared.title: Effect

shared.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
shared.title: Null value

shared.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
shared.title: Observation

shared.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
shared.title: Phase

shared.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
shared.title: Prediction

shared.prose:
The worker runs the selected operation after policy application in an apply worker, or after the unapplied actor's setup:

| Kind / action | Native operation and operation-specific consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `file / open_read` | `open(O_RDONLY)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte read and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; read and close results are discarded. |
| `file / open_write` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_TRUNC)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte `x` write and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; write and close results are discarded. |
| `file / create` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CREAT, 0600)` then close. Creation mode is subject to umask. An existing file is opened without truncation or exclusive creation. |
| `file / read_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_RDONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)`, `fstat`, one read bounded by <!-- span limits.fresh_read_bytes.value_unit -->64 bytes<!-- /span -->, then close. Record each boundary and read bytes; aggregate failure selects stat, read or close failure after a successful open. |
| `file / write_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)` of an existing target, opened `fstat`, `ftruncate(0)`, truncated `fstat`, one-byte `x` write after successful truncation, written `fstat`, then close. Preserve the first failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / create_fresh` | `lstat` before a fresh exclusive `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC \| O_CREAT \| O_EXCL, 0600)`, opened `fstat`, one-byte `x` write, written `fstat`, then close. Pre-open `lstat` is an independent observation. Preserve the first operation failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / unlink` | `unlink(target)` and its return/errno. |
| `file / access` | `access(target, R_OK)` and its return/errno. This is an access-check observation. |
| `mach / lookup` | Obtain the task bootstrap port and call `bootstrap_look_up` for the supplied name; release the returned service port on success. |
| `sysctl / read` | One `sysctlbyname` call with a <!-- span limits.sysctl_read_bytes.value_unit -->4,096 bytes<!-- /span --> buffer acquired after application. Report the call's result and errno; discard value bytes and the returned length. |
| `exec / spawn` | Prepare per-attempt child resources, call `posix_spawn` for the absolute target with the requested argv, then collect child and cleanup observations. |

A short fresh write records its native count and fails the aggregate while retaining zero native errno when the write returned a short nonnegative count. A fresh file descriptor belongs to that attempt and is closed before its result is published.

The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.

facts.free.effect: Dispatch only the admitted kind/action pair, record the operation's native observations and publish its slot after the attempt. Preserve operation-specific success meaning alongside the aggregate result.

nodes.prose: The worker operation implementations and exec setup branches were read. Fresh-file effects, closed-descriptor inheritance, syscall buffers and cleanup behavior still need their existing control runs attached to the release evidence. The legacy open operations intentionally retain their open-boundary aggregate meaning.
nodes.title: Operation controls to attach

nodes.prose:
The worker runs the selected operation after policy application in an apply worker, or after the unapplied actor's setup:

| Kind / action | Native operation and operation-specific consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `file / open_read` | `open(O_RDONLY)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte read and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; read and close results are discarded. |
| `file / open_write` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_TRUNC)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte `x` write and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; write and close results are discarded. |
| `file / create` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CREAT, 0600)` then close. Creation mode is subject to umask. An existing file is opened without truncation or exclusive creation. |
| `file / read_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_RDONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)`, `fstat`, one read bounded by <!-- span limits.fresh_read_bytes.value_unit -->64 bytes<!-- /span -->, then close. Record each boundary and read bytes; aggregate failure selects stat, read or close failure after a successful open. |
| `file / write_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)` of an existing target, opened `fstat`, `ftruncate(0)`, truncated `fstat`, one-byte `x` write after successful truncation, written `fstat`, then close. Preserve the first failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / create_fresh` | `lstat` before a fresh exclusive `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC \| O_CREAT \| O_EXCL, 0600)`, opened `fstat`, one-byte `x` write, written `fstat`, then close. Pre-open `lstat` is an independent observation. Preserve the first operation failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / unlink` | `unlink(target)` and its return/errno. |
| `file / access` | `access(target, R_OK)` and its return/errno. This is an access-check observation. |
| `mach / lookup` | Obtain the task bootstrap port and call `bootstrap_look_up` for the supplied name; release the returned service port on success. |
| `sysctl / read` | One `sysctlbyname` call with a <!-- span limits.sysctl_read_bytes.value_unit -->4,096 bytes<!-- /span --> buffer acquired after application. Report the call's result and errno; discard value bytes and the returned length. |
| `exec / spawn` | Prepare per-attempt child resources, call `posix_spawn` for the absolute target with the requested argv, then collect child and cleanup observations. |

A short fresh write records its native count and fails the aggregate while retaining zero native errno when the write returned a short nonnegative count. A fresh file descriptor belongs to that attempt and is closed before its result is published.

shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.

and asserting cancellation with earlier application observations retained.

shared.prose:
| Operation | Required operands | Producing actor and consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue` | `family`, `target`, `authority`, `token_ref` | Active actor calls native file issuance once with class selected by authority, exact target and flags zero; assigns the declared token resource. |
| `transfer` | `token_ref`, `recipient`, `delivery_ref` | Token-owning actor publishes a host request for one assigned recipient slot; assigns the delivery resource. |
| `consume` | `delivery_ref`, `handle_ref` | Recipient actor calls native consume on its usable delivered token; assigns the handle resource. |
| `release` | `handle_ref` | Consuming actor calls native release for its candidate handle. |

Each other operand must be absent. A required null operand is missing for this grammar; an extraneous null operand is inapplicable.
shared.title: Operation grammar

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
shared.title: Absent field

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
shared.title: Effect

shared.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
shared.title: Null value

shared.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
shared.title: Observation

shared.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
shared.title: Phase

shared.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
shared.title: Prediction

shared.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
shared.title: Request

shared.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
shared.title: Specimen

shared.prose:
Fixed byte length of the CodeDirectory hashes admitted from equipment
inventory and code inspection.
shared.title: CodeDirectory hash byte width

shared.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
shared.title: CodeDirectory hexadecimal width

shared.prose:
Fixed byte length of SHA-256 digests used for the schema fingerprint, worker
identity and signed-file hashes.
shared.title: SHA-256 digest length

shared.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
shared.title: SHA-256 hexadecimal width

shared.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.
shared.title: Exact admission identity

shared.prose: A wait records the host boundary at which it moved on. Budgets and elapsed values use milliseconds on CLOCK_MONOTONIC.
shared.title: Measured host wait

shared.prose: Allowance assigned to this wait; its owning operation defines the cap and whether other work is excluded.
shared.title: budget_ms

shared.prose: Whether the monotonic clock failed or moved backward during this wait.
shared.title: clock_fault

shared.prose: Measured interval at stop. Absence records that the clock could not supply a valid nondecreasing interval.
shared.title: elapsed_ms

shared.prose: Measured synchronous work excluded from this wait's allowance. For sentinel waiting, consumed allowance is elapsed_ms minus excluded_ms; absence means this exclusion is unreported or inapplicable.
shared.title: excluded_ms

shared.prose: Native error captured by the wait's failing prerequisite or observation, when that branch supplies one.
shared.title: native_errno

shared.prose: Owning operation's reason for ending this wait. clock_unavailable denotes failed or backward time with bounded sleep fallback; setup_failed denotes an unavailable nonblocking prerequisite.
shared.title: stop

shared.prose: A gate references the source actor's retained owned_reap instead of copying a second ending.
shared.title: Owned-ending reference

shared.prose: Ordinal of the source actor's owned ending; its association must match that source's owned_reap record.
shared.title: capture_ordinal

shared.prose: Each apply actor owns a separate policy. The host bounds the selected source string and parameter map before starting workers or validators.
shared.title: Worker policy input

shared.prose: Controller-resolved list of named packaged SBPL fragments. Omission, null and an empty list are no-ops. The controller strips the field before delivery. The host accepts the no-op forms and refuses a nonempty unresolved list.
shared.title: augments

shared.prose: When true, request a compiled-profile receipt from the worker before application and require a valid capture_nonce. Omission, null and false leave capture unrequested.
shared.title: capture_compiled_profile

shared.prose: Required with enabled capture: exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding the caller's nonce. A non-null nonce with capture disabled is an inapplicable-field refusal. Receipt publication and consistency checks belong to the compiled-profile surface.
shared.title: capture_nonce

shared.prose: The worker treats a null compiled-profile pointer as failure and proceeds with a non-null pointer. The helper also treats a non-null native diagnostic as failure. A simultaneous profile and diagnostic therefore takes different branches in these producers. Whether to align that behavior, and how to dispose of that diagnostic in the worker branch, remains unresolved.
shared.title: Worker and helper compile classification

shared.prose: The accepted policy representation is `sbpl`; another value is refused before worker launch.
shared.title: format

shared.prose: The parameter teaching examples are preserved from the guide and prior examination. Their native outcomes require the release's helper and worker controls; none is credited as executed by this draft.
shared.title: Parameter example execution

shared.prose:
A source may combine a parameter with a literal suffix:

```scheme
(version 1)
(deny default)
(allow file-read* (literal (string-append (param "ROOT") "/hosts")))
```

`"params":{"ROOT":"/etc"}` supplies the value used by this expression. An unused `OPTIONAL` parameter and a referenced but missing `ROOT` exercise different compiler paths. Inspect the native compile record for the latter's outcome.
shared.title: Parameter expressions

facts.free.effect: Sort parameter keys, transport their complete strings, create native parameters only for a nonempty map, and pass each key and value through sandbox_set_param before compiling the selected source. Report setup or compile failure at the observed native stage.

shared.prose: A supplied parameter is data for the SBPL compiler. The compiler decides how source expressions use it. Source text, selected parameter values and imported file bytes are distinct inputs.
shared.title: Prepare native compiler input

shared.prose: Optional string-to-string compiler parameter map. Omission, null and an empty map produce no native parameter setup. Supplied names remain open data. At most <!-- span limits.policy_parameters.value_unit -->1,024 items<!-- /span --> fit each policy, with keys bounded by <!-- span limits.parameter_key.value_unit -->127 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and values by <!-- span limits.parameter_value.value_unit -->383 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->; native strings must be NUL-free.
shared.title: params

shared.prose: Required string when applying a policy. An empty string reaches native compilation. The final source after augmentation fits <!-- span limits.policy_source.value_unit -->262,143 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->, and embedded NUL is refused before child launch.
shared.title: sbpl_source

shared.prose: A saved specimen describes one experiment. The controller reads its file once, resolves controller options and packaged augments, and serializes the held request delivered to the client. Direct XPC callers supply the host form themselves. The standalone compiler helper accepts its own policy input.
shared.title: Saved specimens and runner selection

shared.prose: These controls are admitted as request data in the current implementation, including packaged hosts. Their names identify test use; the parser applies the documented grammar and capacities.
shared.title: Execution overrides

shared.prose: Actor equipment role-to-path map. Present maps must be nonempty and use only `selected` and `unentitled` keys; actor admission requires absolute paths. The ordinary form refuses this map.
shared.title: actor_equipment_executable_paths

shared.prose: A caller whose connection passes host authorization can supply these controls. Actor equipment preparation checks the packaged inventory and both packaged role bindings before considering fixture override bindings. It retains the packaged and test_override rows with their respective implementation identities.
shared.title: Override admission and equipment ordering

shared.prose: The draft has inspected the decoder and timeout planning. Existing signed-app cases exercise several overrides; a complete mapping of overrides to boundary assertions and applicable release results remains to be assembled, including downstream worker-argument refusal for excessive values. This gap records incomplete evidence attribution across the override set.
shared.title: Override fixture coverage

shared.prose: The signal-number bound 31 remains a source-owned grammar value. Collection floors are selected by the production planning helpers and checked against the limits inventory. The ordinary worker floor and fixture-delay caps have controls calling the production planning helper and argument parser. Actor admission currently accepts worker_timeout_ms although actor execution uses its fixed allowance. Whether to refuse that inapplicable override remains an admission decision.
shared.title: Override quantities and applicability

shared.prose: Validator executable override, bounded by <!-- span limits.test_override_path.value_unit -->1,023 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. The validator remains a separate child and receives query work through its own channel.
shared.title: validator_executable_path

shared.prose: Per-validator I/O timeout override in milliseconds. The host floors the proposed allowance at <!-- span limits.validator_io_override_floor.value_unit -->50 milliseconds<!-- /span -->; omission uses <!-- span limits.validator_io_wait.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The remaining aggregate collection allowance can reduce the effective timeout below that floor.
shared.title: validator_io_timeout_ms

shared.prose: Cumulative validator collection budget override in milliseconds, spanning phases. Both schedulers clamp it to a minimum of <!-- span limits.validator_collection_override_floor.value_unit -->1 millisecond<!-- /span --> and their configured maximum: <!-- span limits.phase_collection_wait.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> for the ordinary form and <!-- span limits.actor_collection_allowance.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> for actors. Omission uses that maximum.
shared.title: validator_total_timeout_ms

shared.prose: Ordinary-worker executable override, bounded by <!-- span limits.test_override_path.value_unit -->1,023 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. Actor-form admission refuses this singular override.
shared.title: worker_executable_path

shared.prose: Nonnegative zero-based slot in each worker's own plan. After that attempt returns and its result payload is written, the worker raises SIGKILL before publishing completion. Negative values are omitted. The worker argument parser requires an index below <!-- span limits.probe_steps.value_unit -->256 items<!-- /span -->; an index beyond the worker's actual plan has no reached action to trigger it.
shared.title: worker_kill_before_publish_slot

shared.prose: Positive fixture delay in milliseconds after all declared visits and actions, before terminal publication. The host forwards positive values; the worker argument parser accepts through <!-- span limits.worker_fixture_delay.value_unit -->60,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. A larger forwarded value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted by the host.
shared.title: worker_post_apply_hang_ms

shared.prose: Positive fixture signal requested after completed actions and before terminal publication, including an unapplied actor's visits. The host forwards positive values; the worker accepts signal numbers through 31. A larger value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted. A signal request can return without termination; final process observations decide the ending.
shared.title: worker_post_apply_kill_signal

shared.prose: Positive fixture delay in milliseconds after compilation and optional capture, before an apply worker's readiness byte and policy application. The host forwards positive values; the worker argument parser accepts through <!-- span limits.worker_fixture_delay.value_unit -->60,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. A larger value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted. The unapplied actor branch bypasses this compile/readiness path.
shared.title: worker_pre_ready_hang_ms

shared.prose: Ordinary worker sentinel budget override in milliseconds. The host floors the supplied allowance at <!-- span limits.worker_timeout_override_floor.value_unit -->50 milliseconds<!-- /span -->; omission uses <!-- span limits.worker_sentinel_wait.value_unit -->120,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. Actor scheduling uses its fixed <!-- span limits.actor_execution_allowance.value_unit -->120,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> allowance even when this field is supplied.
shared.title: worker_timeout_ms

shared.prose: The host request objects have closed field sets. Parameter-map keys and caller labels are data within their own bounds.
shared.title: Specimen

shared.prose: Optional execution controls accepted by the host request decoder. Each declared control retains its stated scope and meaning; unknown override fields are refused.
shared.title: _test_overrides

shared.prose: A non-null actor array selects the actor form; an empty array is refused. Each declared actor has its own fresh worker and at least one declared visit. Omission or null selects the ordinary form.
shared.title: actors

facts.free.effect: Check contract first, decode the selected plan form and closed nested objects, check capacities, then validate policy and plan meaning. A refusal returns bad_request with no worker or validator execution and an empty steps array. A host may already exist to deliver this refusal.

shared.prose: The decoder follows its object and branch order. A capacity failure can precede a semantic failure in a successfully decoded object. Admission accepts or refuses the complete plan; it preserves declared action counts. Empty ordinary plans still compile and apply the policy.
shared.title: Admission order and effects

shared.prose:
This template applies a policy with no probe actions. Replace the assertion with the packaged version's `build.contract` before submission.

```json
{"contract":"<reported-contract>","specimen_id":"apply-only","policy":{"format":"sbpl","sbpl_source":"(version 1) (allow default)"},"probe_plan":[]}
```
shared.title: Apply-only specimen

facts.free.effect: Refuse excess before launch: <!-- span limits.policy_source.value_unit -->262,143 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> per final policy source, <!-- span limits.probe_steps.value_unit -->256 items<!-- /span --> total actions, <!-- span limits.phase_count.value_unit -->8 items<!-- /span --> ordinary phases, and <!-- span limits.actor_phases.value_unit -->16 items<!-- /span --> actor phases. Preserve complete UTF-8 strings at accepted bounds.

shared.prose: Native C-string inputs also refuse embedded NUL. Host-only labels use their declared UTF-8 capacities. Unicode is counted by encoded bytes. A paired query and attempt consumes one action; an extension action consumes one action and contributes no query. Phase and actor counts do not multiply the total action capacity.
shared.title: Bounded strings and action counts

shared.prose: Required non-null string asserting the exact public contract identity. The controller checks it before selector parsing and augmentation; the host checks it before other request fields. Obtain the current value from the packaged version envelope. `unbound` is refused.
shared.title: contract

shared.prose: The exact handling of repeated JSON object keys across the controller parser and Swift decoder still requires a paired boundary control. The closed-field and branch-order obligations above concern the object each decoder produces.
shared.title: Duplicate-key decoding

facts.free.effect: Read and parse the request file once; gate its contract, parse selection, resolve named augments, strip controller selector fields and serialize once for client delivery. Preserve original and selected policy observations in the specimen dossier.

shared.title: Hold and deliver the selected request

facts.free.effect: Treat optional null as absent where decodeIfPresent is used. Refuse present null for actor equipment, actor required_entitlements, after_termination and actor_equipment_executable_paths. Retain presence of extension operands so an inapplicable operand is refused even when null.

shared.prose: Ordered phase declarations. The ordinary form requires a nonempty array, forbids actor ownership, termination dependencies and extension actions, and uses one worker across its phases. The actor form requires phases and forbids a non-null `probe_plan`.
shared.title: phases

shared.prose: Policy for the ordinary form. With no non-null `actors`, the policy object is required. In the actor form a non-null top-level policy is refused; each actor declares its own sandbox mode and policy.
shared.title: policy

shared.prose: Ordinary paired probes, including an empty array for apply-only execution. Exactly one of this field and `phases` must be non-null in the ordinary form. The host represents this plan as the `main` phase.
shared.title: probe_plan

shared.prose: Optional caller label, bounded by <!-- span limits.request_label.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. Omission and null have the same meaning; it selects no execution mode.
shared.title: run_kind

shared.prose: Required non-null string caller label, echoed when it fits <!-- span limits.specimen_id.value_unit -->255 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. It may be empty. Its identity is independent of the worker PID or an actor ID.
shared.title: specimen_id

nodes.prose: An action is one JSON object in the phase actions array. The decoder chooses an extension action when the `extension` key is present; otherwise it decodes a paired probe. A present null extension therefore selects extension decoding and fails its required object.
nodes.title: Phase action variants

nodes.prose: The ordinary and actor forms currently differ on empty step IDs. Aligning them requires an explicit admission decision; this draft preserves the implemented distinction.
nodes.title: Empty ordinary identifiers

nodes.prose: The extension variant is `PWRunnerExtensionAction`: a step ID and closed extension operation, as defined by the extensions surface. It contributes no sandbox query.
nodes.title: Extension action

facts.free.effect: Refuse repeated step IDs across the complete specimen. Actor actions require nonempty IDs. The ordinary form currently accepts an empty step ID when it is unique.

nodes.prose: The probe variant is `PWRunnerProbeStep`: a step ID, sandbox query and attempt, as defined by the probes surface.
nodes.title: Paired probe

nodes.prose: A specimen admits at most <!-- span limits.actors.value_unit -->8 items<!-- /span -->. Each actor has at least one declared phase. Each required-entitlement list fits <!-- span limits.actor_required_entitlements.value_unit -->64 items<!-- /span -->, with each key bounded by <!-- span limits.actor_entitlement_key.value_unit -->255 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->.
nodes.title: Actor declaration

nodes.prose: Nonempty specimen-local actor identifier, unique across actors and bounded by <!-- span limits.actor_id.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. Native transport also requires NUL-free bytes.
nodes.title: actor_id

nodes.prose: Equipment role: `selected` uses the selected runner worker; `unentitled` uses the packaged unentitled worker. Omission selects `selected`; present null is refused.
nodes.title: equipment

facts.free.effect: Launch one fresh worker for each actor. An apply worker compiles and applies its own declared policy once before its visits; an unapplied worker publishes that declaration and executes under the restrictions already inherited by its process. Keep that worker for its successive visits.

Require unique nonempty actor IDs, known equipment roles, valid sandbox declarations, valid entitlement demands, and at least one phase per actor. Build one resolved plan whose actor and resource indexes govern execution.

nodes.prose: Static and live read-back demand for boolean-true entitlement keys on this actor's executable. Omission supplies an empty list; present null is refused. Keys must be nonempty and unique.
nodes.title: required_entitlements

nodes.prose: The actor's explicit apply or unapplied declaration; application assessment is reported separately from this request.
nodes.title: sandbox

nodes.prose: The declaration names a source actor, while the gate reports the host's owned observation of its ending.
nodes.title: Termination dependency

nodes.prose: Known actor whose final declared phase occurs earlier than the dependent phase. It must differ from the dependent phase's actor.
nodes.title: actor_id

facts.free.effect: At admission require the source's final declared visit before the dependent phase. Before activating the dependent actor or collecting its predictions, evaluate the owned natural-reap gate. A failed evaluated gate cancels every remaining scheduled phase.

nodes.prose: The actor form admits <!-- span limits.actor_phases.value_unit -->16 items<!-- /span --> and the ordinary form <!-- span limits.phase_count.value_unit -->8 items<!-- /span -->. Across either form, actions share the <!-- span limits.probe_steps.value_unit -->256 items<!-- /span --> total capacity.
nodes.title: Phase declaration

nodes.prose: Actions in declaration order, including an empty array. Ordinary phases contain paired probes. Actor phases may also contain extension actions. Action identifiers are unique across the whole specimen.
nodes.title: actions

nodes.prose: Required known actor owner in the actor form. The ordinary form requires absence or null.
nodes.title: actor_id

nodes.prose: Optional owned-termination dependency in the actor form. Absence supplies no dependency; present null is refused. The ordinary form refuses a supplied dependency.
nodes.title: after_termination

nodes.prose: The phase-order source has been inspected in the wider examination. Integrated order-barrier and mutation controls must be attached to the completed release account; this draft credits no execution of those controls.
nodes.title: Barrier execution evidence

facts.free.effect: Close the active phase's eligible prediction collection before releasing its actions; run those actions in declaration order. Begin the next phase's collection after the previous phase completes. In the actor form activate one actor at a time while other workers remain parked.

nodes.prose: Nonempty identifier unique across the specimen's phases and bounded by <!-- span limits.phase_id.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and NUL-free.
nodes.title: phase_id

nodes.prose: `apply` requires a policy and asks the worker to compile/apply it; `unapplied` requires policy absence or null and records the inherited process restrictions as its starting condition.
nodes.title: mode

nodes.prose: Required non-null policy for `apply`; a non-null policy is refused for `unapplied`. Each apply policy has its own source, parameters, augmentation and capture request.
nodes.title: policy

shared.prose: The host classifies the apply-call boundary from mode, launch, applied publication, eligible authority failure and terminal worker evidence, in that precedence order.

shared.prose: The specific declaration, launch state or worker/authority publication supporting state. The eleven permitted state/basis pairs are defined by the application rule below.
shared.title: basis

Final actor collection preserves a later applied publication and derives

needs an owning behavioral check; the current account is supported by source.

shared.prose: not_requested, not_attempted, observed or unobserved. observed identifies evidence of the apply boundary, including a native apply failure; unobserved retains an unresolved result.

shared.prose: The gate belongs to the dependent phase and observes the named source actor after that source’s final scheduled visit was activated.

shared.prose:
The dependency wait observes the owned source child without requesting its
departure. Its budget is the lesser of <!-- span limits.actor_termination_wait.value_unit -->5,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> and the remaining
execution allowance in whole milliseconds. Deadline samples and final elapsed
accounting govern satisfaction. These are charged-wait conditions; operating
system scheduling determines when the host next runs.

A failed evaluated gate sets `schedule.cancelled` to
`termination_dependency:<outcome>`. Later phases retain their declarations
with collection `not_reached`, false arrival/completion and absent activation
and visit timing. Their own gates remain `not_reached`. Final cleanup may add
the source's later owned ending while the failed gate keeps the observation
reference captured during its evaluation.

Mismatch or inspection failure cancels all scheduling, retains earlier setup/application publications and leaves all phases unactivated and uncollected. An unavailable setup can coexist with other usable actors when no inspection failure cancels them.

shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.
shared.title: Associating the owned process

shared.prose:
The read unit controls construct failing Security-call results and verify the
retained attempted prefix and ineligible execution. The signed-product
acceptance evidence still needs a case reaching runtime inspection failure
and asserting cancellation with earlier application observations retained.
The optional additional deadline after an unavailable orchestration clock sample is source-read; this draft credits no control of that initial failure followed by valid inspection clocks.
shared.title: Live-inspection evidence limit

shared.title: native_observations

shared.prose: Host monotonic observation time in nanoseconds. A matched record requires valid inspection start and final clock samples, a nondecreasing final time, and both samples before the additional inspection deadline when that deadline was established. The scheduler separately guards the shared setup allowance.
shared.title: observed_at_monotonic_ns

shared.prose:
| Operation | Required operands | Producing actor and consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue` | `family`, `target`, `authority`, `token_ref` | Active actor calls native file issuance once with class selected by authority, exact target and flags zero; assigns the declared token resource. |
| `transfer` | `token_ref`, `recipient`, `delivery_ref` | Token-owning actor publishes a host request for one assigned recipient slot; assigns the delivery resource. |
| `consume` | `delivery_ref`, `handle_ref` | Recipient actor calls native consume on its usable delivered token; assigns the handle resource. |
| `release` | `handle_ref` | Consuming actor calls native release for its candidate handle. |

Each other operand must be absent. A required null operand is missing for this grammar; an extraneous null operand is inapplicable.
