shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
shared.title: Absent field

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
shared.title: Effect

shared.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
shared.title: Null value

shared.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
shared.title: Observation

shared.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
shared.title: Phase

shared.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
shared.title: Prediction

shared.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
shared.title: Request

shared.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
shared.title: Specimen

shared.prose:
Fixed byte length of the CodeDirectory hashes admitted from equipment
inventory and code inspection.
shared.title: CodeDirectory hash byte width

shared.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
shared.title: CodeDirectory hexadecimal width

shared.prose:
Fixed byte length of SHA-256 digests used for the schema fingerprint, worker
identity and signed-file hashes.
shared.title: SHA-256 digest length

shared.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
shared.title: SHA-256 hexadecimal width

shared.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.
shared.title: Exact admission identity

shared.prose: A wait records the host boundary at which it moved on. Budgets and elapsed values use milliseconds on CLOCK_MONOTONIC.
shared.title: Measured host wait

shared.prose: Allowance assigned to this wait; its owning operation defines the cap and whether other work is excluded.
shared.title: budget_ms

shared.prose: Whether the monotonic clock failed or moved backward during this wait.
shared.title: clock_fault

shared.prose: Measured interval at stop. Absence records that the clock could not supply a valid nondecreasing interval.
shared.title: elapsed_ms

shared.prose: Measured synchronous work excluded from this wait's allowance. For sentinel waiting, consumed allowance is elapsed_ms minus excluded_ms; absence means this exclusion is unreported or inapplicable.
shared.title: excluded_ms

shared.prose: Native error captured by the wait's failing prerequisite or observation, when that branch supplies one.
shared.title: native_errno

shared.prose: Owning operation's reason for ending this wait. clock_unavailable denotes failed or backward time with bounded sleep fallback; setup_failed denotes an unavailable nonblocking prerequisite.
shared.title: stop

shared.prose: A gate references the source actor's retained owned_reap instead of copying a second ending.
shared.title: Owned-ending reference

shared.prose: Ordinal of the source actor's owned ending; its association must match that source's owned_reap record.
shared.title: capture_ordinal

shared.prose: Each apply actor owns a separate policy. The host bounds the selected source string and parameter map before starting workers or validators.
shared.title: Worker policy input

shared.prose: Controller-resolved list of named packaged SBPL fragments. Omission, null and an empty list are no-ops. The controller strips the field before delivery. The host accepts the no-op forms and refuses a nonempty unresolved list.
shared.title: augments

shared.prose: When true, request a compiled-profile receipt from the worker before application and require a valid capture_nonce. Omission, null and false leave capture unrequested.
shared.title: capture_compiled_profile

shared.prose: Required with enabled capture: exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters encoding the caller's nonce. A non-null nonce with capture disabled is an inapplicable-field refusal. Receipt publication and consistency checks belong to the compiled-profile surface.
shared.title: capture_nonce

shared.prose: The worker treats a null compiled-profile pointer as failure and proceeds with a non-null pointer. The helper also treats a non-null native diagnostic as failure. A simultaneous profile and diagnostic therefore takes different branches in these producers. Whether to align that behavior, and how to dispose of that diagnostic in the worker branch, remains unresolved.
shared.title: Worker and helper compile classification

shared.prose: The accepted policy representation is `sbpl`; another value is refused before worker launch.
shared.title: format

shared.prose: The parameter teaching examples are preserved from the guide and prior examination. Their native outcomes require the release's helper and worker controls; none is credited as executed by this draft.
shared.title: Parameter example execution

shared.prose:
A source may combine a parameter with a literal suffix:

```scheme
(version 1)
(deny default)
(allow file-read* (literal (string-append (param "ROOT") "/hosts")))
```

`"params":{"ROOT":"/etc"}` supplies the value used by this expression. An unused `OPTIONAL` parameter and a referenced but missing `ROOT` exercise different compiler paths. Inspect the native compile record for the latter's outcome.
shared.title: Parameter expressions

facts.free.effect: Sort parameter keys, transport their complete strings, create native parameters only for a nonempty map, and pass each key and value through sandbox_set_param before compiling the selected source. Report setup or compile failure at the observed native stage.

shared.prose: A supplied parameter is data for the SBPL compiler. The compiler decides how source expressions use it. Source text, selected parameter values and imported file bytes are distinct inputs.
shared.title: Prepare native compiler input

shared.prose: Optional string-to-string compiler parameter map. Omission, null and an empty map produce no native parameter setup. Supplied names remain open data. At most <!-- span limits.policy_parameters.value_unit -->1,024 items<!-- /span --> fit each policy, with keys bounded by <!-- span limits.parameter_key.value_unit -->127 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and values by <!-- span limits.parameter_value.value_unit -->383 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->; native strings must be NUL-free.
shared.title: params

shared.prose: Required string when applying a policy. An empty string reaches native compilation. The final source after augmentation fits <!-- span limits.policy_source.value_unit -->262,143 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->, and embedded NUL is refused before child launch.
shared.title: sbpl_source

shared.prose: Closed action within its family, listed in the operation table below. An unsupported pair refuses the complete request before children.
shared.title: action

shared.prose: Exec-only argument strings appended after target as argv[0]. Omission and null mean an empty list. A supplied array on another kind, including an empty array, is refused. At most <!-- span limits.exec_arguments.value_unit -->15 items<!-- /span --> are admitted, each NUL-free and bounded by <!-- span limits.exec_argument.value_unit -->127 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->.
shared.title: args

facts.free.effect: After application or an actor's unapplied declaration, acquire stdout/stderr pipes and spawn actions for this released attempt, release them on setup failure and at completion, and report the failing setup call when spawning was prevented. Spawn with target as argv[0], an empty environment, /dev/null stdin, captured stdout/stderr, close-on-exec descriptor policy and a new process group.

shared.prose: A successful spawn supplies a child PID even if the child later exits nonzero. The child collection, termination request and owned reap remain separate observations. The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.

shared.prose:
The worker runs the selected operation after policy application in an apply worker, or after the unapplied actor's setup:

| Kind / action | Native operation and operation-specific consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `file / open_read` | `open(O_RDONLY)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte read and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; read and close results are discarded. |
| `file / open_write` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_TRUNC)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte `x` write and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; write and close results are discarded. |
| `file / create` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CREAT, 0600)` then close. Creation mode is subject to umask. An existing file is opened without truncation or exclusive creation. |
| `file / read_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_RDONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)`, `fstat`, one read bounded by <!-- span limits.fresh_read_bytes.value_unit -->64 bytes<!-- /span -->, then close. Record each boundary and read bytes; aggregate failure selects stat, read or close failure after a successful open. |
| `file / write_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)` of an existing target, opened `fstat`, `ftruncate(0)`, truncated `fstat`, one-byte `x` write after successful truncation, written `fstat`, then close. Preserve the first failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / create_fresh` | `lstat` before a fresh exclusive `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC \| O_CREAT \| O_EXCL, 0600)`, opened `fstat`, one-byte `x` write, written `fstat`, then close. Pre-open `lstat` is an independent observation. Preserve the first operation failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / unlink` | `unlink(target)` and its return/errno. |
| `file / access` | `access(target, R_OK)` and its return/errno. This is an access-check observation. |
| `mach / lookup` | Obtain the task bootstrap port and call `bootstrap_look_up` for the supplied name; release the returned service port on success. |
| `sysctl / read` | One `sysctlbyname` call with a <!-- span limits.sysctl_read_bytes.value_unit -->4,096 bytes<!-- /span --> buffer acquired after application. Report the call's result and errno; discard value bytes and the returned length. |
| `exec / spawn` | Prepare per-attempt child resources, call `posix_spawn` for the absolute target with the requested argv, then collect child and cleanup observations. |

A short fresh write records its native count and fails the aggregate while retaining zero native errno when the write returned a short nonnegative count. A fresh file descriptor belongs to that attempt and is closed before its result is published.

nodes.prose:
Declare actors `issuer` and `reader`. Choose the issuer's equipment and sandbox policy to exercise issuance authority, and a reader policy whose baseline denies the chosen path. Use an exact absolute target:

| Phase owner | Actions in declaration order |
| --- | --- |
| `reader` | `read_fresh` before receiving authority |
| `issuer` | issue `token_ref: "t"`, family `file`, authority `read`; transfer `t` to `reader` as `delivery_ref: "d"` |
| `reader` | consume `d` as `handle_ref: "h"`; `read_fresh`; release `h`; `read_fresh` again |

The first read supplies the baseline. The middle read supplies access during this handle's lifetime. The last read supplies a later access observation after the native release call. Compare their actual file identity and content observations. A non-null issue result, delivered bytes, consume result and release result each remain visible even when a read fails.

shared.prose:
The dependency wait observes the owned source child without requesting its
departure. Its budget is the lesser of <!-- span limits.actor_termination_wait.value_unit -->5,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> and the remaining
execution allowance in whole milliseconds. Deadline samples and final elapsed
accounting govern satisfaction. These are charged-wait conditions; operating
system scheduling determines when the host next runs.

A failed evaluated gate sets `schedule.cancelled` to
`termination_dependency:<outcome>`. Later phases retain their declarations
with collection `not_reached`, false arrival/completion and absent activation
and visit timing. Their own gates remain `not_reached`. Final cleanup may add
the source's later owned ending while the failed gate keeps the observation
reference captured during its evaluation.

shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.
shared.title: Associating the owned process

The read unit controls construct failing Security-call results and verify the
retained attempted prefix and ineligible execution. The signed-product
acceptance evidence still needs a case reaching runtime inspection failure
and asserting cancellation with earlier application observations retained.
The optional additional deadline after an unavailable orchestration clock sample is source-read; this draft credits no control of that initial failure followed by valid inspection clocks.

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
shared.title: Absent field

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
shared.title: Effect

shared.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
shared.title: Null value

shared.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
shared.title: Observation

shared.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
shared.title: Phase

shared.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
shared.title: Prediction

shared.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
shared.title: Request

shared.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
shared.title: Specimen

Fixed byte length of the CodeDirectory hashes admitted from equipment
inventory and code inspection.

identity and signed-file hashes.

A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.

A simultaneous profile and diagnostic therefore takes different branches in these producers. Whether to align that behavior, and how to dispose of that diagnostic in the worker branch, remains unresolved.

shared.prose:
A source may combine a parameter with a literal suffix:

```scheme
(version 1)
(deny default)
(allow file-read* (literal (string-append (param "ROOT") "/hosts")))
```

`"params":{"ROOT":"/etc"}` supplies the value used by this expression. An unused `OPTIONAL` parameter and a referenced but missing `ROOT` exercise different compiler paths. Inspect the native compile record for the latter's outcome.

facts.free.effect: Sort parameter keys, transport their complete strings, create native parameters only for a nonempty map, and pass each key and value through sandbox_set_param before compiling the selected source. Report setup or compile failure at the observed native stage.

shared.prose: A supplied parameter is data for the SBPL compiler. The compiler decides how source expressions use it. Source text, selected parameter values and imported file bytes are distinct inputs.
shared.title: Prepare native compiler input

shared.prose: Optional string-to-string compiler parameter map. Omission, null and an empty map produce no native parameter setup. Supplied names remain open data. At most <!-- span limits.policy_parameters.value_unit -->1,024 items<!-- /span --> fit each policy, with keys bounded by <!-- span limits.parameter_key.value_unit -->127 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and values by <!-- span limits.parameter_value.value_unit -->383 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->; native strings must be NUL-free.

shared.prose: Closed action within its family, listed in the operation table below. An unsupported pair refuses the complete request before children.

shared.prose: Exec-only argument strings appended after target as argv[0]. Omission and null mean an empty list. A supplied array on another kind, including an empty array, is refused. At most <!-- span limits.exec_arguments.value_unit -->15 items<!-- /span --> are admitted, each NUL-free and bounded by <!-- span limits.exec_argument.value_unit -->127 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->.

facts.free.effect: After application or an actor's unapplied declaration, acquire stdout/stderr pipes and spawn actions for this released attempt, release them on setup failure and at completion, and report the failing setup call when spawning was prevented. Spawn with target as argv[0], an empty environment, /dev/null stdin, captured stdout/stderr, close-on-exec descriptor policy and a new process group.

shared.prose: A successful spawn supplies a child PID even if the child later exits nonzero. The child collection, termination request and owned reap remain separate observations. The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.
shared.title: Exec setup and child inputs

facts.free.effect: Dispatch only the admitted kind/action pair, record the operation's native observations and publish its slot after the attempt. Preserve operation-specific success meaning alongside the aggregate result.
Refuse exec probes in every actor participating in an extension operation, including an actor named only as a transfer recipient. Other actors may declare exec probes.

shared.prose: Native operation family selected with action.
shared.title: kind

shared.prose: The worker operation implementations and exec setup branches were read. Fresh-file effects, closed-descriptor inheritance, syscall buffers and cleanup behavior still need their existing control runs attached to the release evidence. The legacy open operations intentionally retain their open-boundary aggregate meaning.
shared.title: Operation controls to attach

shared.prose:
The worker runs the selected operation after policy application in an apply worker, or after the unapplied actor's setup:

| Kind / action | Native operation and operation-specific consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `file / open_read` | `open(O_RDONLY)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte read and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; read and close results are discarded. |
| `file / open_write` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_TRUNC)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte `x` write and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; write and close results are discarded. |
| `file / create` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CREAT, 0600)` then close. Creation mode is subject to umask. An existing file is opened without truncation or exclusive creation. |
| `file / read_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_RDONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)`, `fstat`, one read bounded by <!-- span limits.fresh_read_bytes.value_unit -->64 bytes<!-- /span -->, then close. Record each boundary and read bytes; aggregate failure selects stat, read or close failure after a successful open. |
| `file / write_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)` of an existing target, opened `fstat`, `ftruncate(0)`, truncated `fstat`, one-byte `x` write after successful truncation, written `fstat`, then close. Preserve the first failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / create_fresh` | `lstat` before a fresh exclusive `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC \| O_CREAT \| O_EXCL, 0600)`, opened `fstat`, one-byte `x` write, written `fstat`, then close. Pre-open `lstat` is an independent observation. Preserve the first operation failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / unlink` | `unlink(target)` and its return/errno. |
| `file / access` | `access(target, R_OK)` and its return/errno. This is an access-check observation. |
| `mach / lookup` | Obtain the task bootstrap port and call `bootstrap_look_up` for the supplied name; release the returned service port on success. |
| `sysctl / read` | One `sysctlbyname` call with a <!-- span limits.sysctl_read_bytes.value_unit -->4,096 bytes<!-- /span --> buffer acquired after application. Report the call's result and errno; discard value bytes and the returned length. |
| `exec / spawn` | Prepare per-attempt child resources, call `posix_spawn` for the absolute target with the requested argv, then collect child and cleanup observations. |

A short fresh write records its native count and fails the aggregate while retaining zero native errno when the write returned a short nonnegative count. A fresh file descriptor belongs to that attempt and is closed before its result is published.
shared.title: Native operations

shared.prose: Operation target, bounded by <!-- span limits.attempt_target.value_unit -->511 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and NUL-free. Exec requires an absolute path. Other admitted targets retain their supplied native-operation meaning.

For an admitted query, withhold native prediction when its path fails host realpath planning or its operation/filter pair is excluded; report prediction_unavailable while leaving the attempt eligible.

| `iokit-open-service` | `iokit_registry_entry_class` |
| `iokit-open-user-client` | `iokit_user_client_class` |


The standalone compiler helper accepts its own policy input.

nodes.prose: A paired probe can query `file-write-create` with a path that does not exist at planning time, then attempt `file/create` at that path. Later realpath diagnostics can resolve a path the earlier query planner could not resolve.

nodes.prose:
Given a correctly asserted ordinary specimen, a policy member `capture_compiled_profiel` is an unknown field. The host returns `bad_request`, with code `unknown_field` and path `["policy","capture_compiled_profiel"]`; the controller exits 1. A worker or validator is not launched for this refusal. Correcting the spelling to `capture_compiled_profile: true` also requires a valid `capture_nonce`.

A target-absence check made by a teaching control is separate evidence of the file state. The structured refusal identifies the stopped admission boundary.

Worker or validator launch failure belongs to the respective child record. A missing completed slot leaves its operation result unresolved. `runner_reporting_failed` carries the reporting failure's explicit retention account and original summary when available. Preserve the records that were actually received while reading each failure at its own scope.

nodes.prose:
| Category | Current code examples and condition |
| --- | --- |
| JSON and required values | `invalid_json`, `invalid_value`, `missing_field`, `missing_value`, `type_mismatch`; decoder structure or required-value failure. |
| Public identity and closed objects | `unsupported_contract`; assertion differs or expected identity is unbound. `unknown_field`; undeclared object key. |
| Plan form and identifiers | `exclusive_plan_forms`, `actors_require_phases`, `empty_phases`, `empty_actors`, `empty_actor_id`, `empty_phase_id`, `empty_step_id`, `duplicate_actor_id`, `duplicate_phase_id`, `duplicate_step_id`, `actor_without_phases`. |
| Policy and query | `unresolved_augments`, `unsupported_policy_format`, `missing_policy_source`, `invalid_capture_nonce`, `empty_operation`, `unknown_filter_kind`, `missing_filter_value`. |
| Attempt and applicability | `unsupported_attempt`, `relative_exec_target`, `inapplicable_field`. Inapplicability includes non-exec args, ordinary actor-only fields, disabled-capture nonce and extraneous extension operands. |
| Actor and equipment | `unsupported_sandbox_mode`, `unsupported_equipment`, `unknown_actor`, `empty_entitlement`, `duplicate_entitlement`, `invalid_termination_dependency`, `empty_equipment_overrides`, `relative_equipment_path`. |
| Extension grammar and ownership | `unsupported_extension_action`, `unsupported_extension_family`, `unsupported_extension_authority`, `relative_extension_target`, `empty_reference`, `duplicate_reference`, `unknown_token_reference`, `unknown_delivery_reference`, `unknown_handle_reference`, `wrong_owner_reference`, `repeated_release` and `extension_exec_unsupported` for reference assignment, ownership, release and exec participation. |
| Capacity | `admission_refused`; exact count, unit and available association are in admission_failure. |

Each code's condition remains attached to its owning input rule. This list supplies current examples for the open code vocabulary.

shared.prose:
The dependency wait observes the owned source child without requesting its
departure. Its budget is the lesser of <!-- span limits.actor_termination_wait.value_unit -->5,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> and the remaining
execution allowance in whole milliseconds. Deadline samples and final elapsed
accounting govern satisfaction. These are charged-wait conditions; operating
system scheduling determines when the host next runs.

A failed evaluated gate sets `schedule.cancelled` to
`termination_dependency:<outcome>`. Later phases retain their declarations
with collection `not_reached`, false arrival/completion and absent activation
and visit timing. Their own gates remain `not_reached`. Final cleanup may add
the source's later owned ending while the failed gate keeps the observation
reference captured during its evaluation.

was unavailable or moved backward. Retained fields provide the available
context for this timing failure.

allowance check that stops traversal earlier leaves the gate `not_reached`.

Cancellation, exhausted schedule allowance or an unavailable dependent actor
or visit stopped traversal before this gate was evaluated. Its wait,

otherwise eligible phases remain schedulable.

Ownership is unbroken, departure_requested is false, budget is positive, deadline samples permit the reap, and final wait has a valid elapsed interval at most budget.

The gate closes after the source's owned ending. A normal exit or signaled
ending can qualify; natural means the host had not requested departure.
Source final-phase completion is a separate observation from activation and

An apply worker compiles and applies its own declared policy once before its visits; an unapplied worker publishes that declaration and executes under the restrictions already inherited by its process. shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.
shared.title: Associating the owned process

shared.prose:

acceptance evidence still needs a case reaching runtime inspection failure
and asserting cancellation with earlier application observations retained.
The optional additional deadline after an unavailable orchestration clock sample is source-read; this draft credits no control of that initial failure followed by valid inspection clocks.

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
shared.title: Absent field

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
shared.title: Effect

shared.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
shared.title: Null value

shared.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
shared.title: Observation

shared.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
shared.title: Phase

shared.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
shared.title: Prediction

shared.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
shared.title: Request

shared.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
shared.title: Specimen

inventory and code inspection.

identity and signed-file hashes.

shared.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.
shared.title: Exact admission identity

shared.prose: A wait records the host boundary at which it moved on. Budgets and elapsed values use milliseconds on CLOCK_MONOTONIC.

shared.title: Augment semantics and historical environment

shared.prose:
`exec_baseline` appends these source rules:

```scheme
(allow process-exec*)
(allow process-fork)
(allow file-read*)
```

The `file-read*` allowance is unconditional. Using this augment changes the selected policy's file-read authority and can mask the denial a file-read experiment intended to observe. Its documented derivation used macOS 14.8.3, build 23J220, and the repository's dynamic exec helper.
shared.title: Packaged exec baseline

facts.free.effect: For a nonempty augment list require a string source, validate every name, read the named resources in requested order and append a newline plus each fragment. Replace the policy source only after every requested read succeeds. Remove augments from the held policy before submission.

Invalid names produce `invalid_augment_name`. A wrong list or element type produces `type_mismatch`. The original file remains unchanged because resolution edits the held JSON value.

A simultaneous profile and diagnostic therefore takes different branches in these producers. Whether to align that behavior, and how to dispose of that diagnostic in the worker branch, remains unresolved.

```scheme

(deny default)

```

`"params":{"ROOT":"/etc"}` supplies the value used by this expression. An unused `OPTIONAL` parameter and a referenced but missing `ROOT` exercise different compiler paths. Inspect the native compile record for the latter's outcome.

At most <!-- span limits.policy_parameters.value_unit -->1,024 items<!-- /span --> fit each policy, with keys bounded by <!-- span limits.parameter_key.value_unit -->127 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and values by <!-- span limits.parameter_value.value_unit -->383 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->; native strings must be NUL-free.

Spawn with target as argv[0], an empty environment, /dev/null stdin, captured stdout/stderr, close-on-exec descriptor policy and a new process group.

shared.prose: A successful spawn supplies a child PID even if the child later exits nonzero. The child collection, termination request and owned reap remain separate observations. The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.

facts.free.effect: Dispatch only the admitted kind/action pair, record the operation's native observations and publish its slot after the attempt. Preserve operation-specific success meaning alongside the aggregate result.
Refuse exec probes in every actor participating in an extension operation, including an actor named only as a transfer recipient. Other actors may declare exec probes.

shared.prose: The worker operation implementations and exec setup branches were read. Fresh-file effects, closed-descriptor inheritance, syscall buffers and cleanup behavior still need their existing control runs attached to the release evidence. The legacy open operations intentionally retain their open-boundary aggregate meaning.
shared.title: Operation controls to attach

shared.prose:
The worker runs the selected operation after policy application in an apply worker, or after the unapplied actor's setup:

| Kind / action | Native operation and operation-specific consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `file / open_read` | `open(O_RDONLY)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte read and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; read and close results are discarded. |
| `file / open_write` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_TRUNC)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte `x` write and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; write and close results are discarded. |
| `file / create` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CREAT, 0600)` then close. Creation mode is subject to umask. An existing file is opened without truncation or exclusive creation. |
| `file / read_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_RDONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)`, `fstat`, one read bounded by <!-- span limits.fresh_read_bytes.value_unit -->64 bytes<!-- /span -->, then close. Record each boundary and read bytes; aggregate failure selects stat, read or close failure after a successful open. |
| `file / write_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)` of an existing target, opened `fstat`, `ftruncate(0)`, truncated `fstat`, one-byte `x` write after successful truncation, written `fstat`, then close. Preserve the first failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / create_fresh` | `lstat` before a fresh exclusive `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC \| O_CREAT \| O_EXCL, 0600)`, opened `fstat`, one-byte `x` write, written `fstat`, then close. Pre-open `lstat` is an independent observation. Preserve the first operation failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / unlink` | `unlink(target)` and its return/errno. |
| `file / access` | `access(target, R_OK)` and its return/errno. This is an access-check observation. |
| `mach / lookup` | Obtain the task bootstrap port and call `bootstrap_look_up` for the supplied name; release the returned service port on success. |
| `sysctl / read` | One `sysctlbyname` call with a <!-- span limits.sysctl_read_bytes.value_unit -->4,096 bytes<!-- /span --> buffer acquired after application. Report the call's result and errno; discard value bytes and the returned length. |
| `exec / spawn` | Prepare per-attempt child resources, call `posix_spawn` for the absolute target with the requested argv, then collect child and cleanup observations. |

A short fresh write records its native count and fails the aggregate while retaining zero native errno when the write returned a short nonnegative count. A fresh file descriptor belongs to that attempt and is closed before its result is published.
shared.title: Native operations

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
The runner client acquires a reservation, submits the held request over XPC
and returns a typed capture of its transport observations and received host
bytes. The controller invokes it once for a run.
shared.title: Runner client

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
The XPC host admits the request, prepares worker resources, coordinates query
collection and action release, collects worker/validator observations and
produces the host reply. Specimen policy application occurs in the worker so
the host retains its reply path.
shared.title: Runner host

shared.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.

The bound reader compares the client’s contract or host producer contract with the caller’s expected public identity; `unbound` cannot supply a positive identity admission. Successful structural decoding establishes the declared typed shape. Native-operation, lifecycle, phase, actor, equipment and custody consistency have separately named semantic readers.

nodes.prose: The frame cap is <!-- span limits.porcelain_frame_bytes.value_unit -->134,217,728 bytes<!-- /span --> and the nesting limit is <!-- span limits.porcelain_nesting.value -->32<!-- /span --> values. Rust shares one <!-- span limits.porcelain_decoded_storage_bytes.value_unit -->134,217,728 bytes<!-- /span --> logical decoded-storage budget across collection slots, strings and byte arrays within each frame; slot charges use the compiled destination type’s size. Capture and embedded host reply are separate frames and separate budgets. Swift bounds encoded values and record growth so a produced frame fits its frame cap. The client retains at most <!-- span limits.client_reply_retention.value_unit -->96,468,992 bytes<!-- /span --> of a host reply. The controller collects client output before applying its <!-- span limits.controller_output.value_unit -->285,212,672 bytes<!-- /span --> per-stream retention cap. These quantities describe distinct allocation, encoding and retention operations; complete-output collection can use more memory than a retained prefix.
nodes.title: Receiver and writer budgets

nodes.prose: A frame is the four ASCII bytes `PWP1`, 32 raw bytes of the schema SHA-256 fingerprint, then exactly one root value. A value is a one-byte kind, a four-byte unsigned little-endian payload length, and exactly that many payload bytes. Every multi-byte integer in the frame grammar is little-endian. Root, record and field identities are those of the declared wire schema retained with the wire surface’s canonical shape.
nodes.title: Frame and value headers

nodes.prose: The fingerprint is SHA-256 of the compact, object-key-sorted JSON wire identity emitted by `wire_identity`: schema version; records in schema order with ID, name and fields; each field’s tag, public name, type descriptor, null rule and any byte projection; path-form and conditional-null rules; root names mapped to record IDs; and declared variant cases. Local-only fields are omitted. Source paths, mutable/default annotations and descriptive text remain source provenance. Changes to a field’s name, tag, type, optionality, null/projection rule or a newly added optional field change the fingerprint and require exact receiver agreement.
nodes.title: Exact wire identity

nodes.prose:
| Kind | Payload and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| 1 · boolean | Exactly one byte: 0 means false and 1 means true. |
| 2 · signed integer | Exactly eight bytes, two’s-complement signed 64-bit. The declared destination type also constrains its representable range. |
| 3 · unsigned integer | Exactly eight bytes, unsigned 64-bit. The declared destination type also constrains its representable range. |
| 4 · text | Strict UTF-8 bytes of the string; payload length supplies its extent. |
| 5 · bytes | Uninterpreted octets. The owning field supplies their public JSON spelling. |
| 6 · record | Unsigned two-byte record ID, then repeated unsigned two-byte field tag and complete value pairs. Tags are nonzero and strictly increasing. |
| 7 · list | Unsigned four-byte element count, followed by that many complete values of the schema’s element type. |
| 8 · ordered string map | Unsigned four-byte entry count, followed by text-key/value pairs. Keys are unique and strictly increasing by their UTF-8 bytes; values have the declared homogeneous type. |
| 9 · declared variant | Unsigned two-byte case tag, followed by exactly one complete value of that case’s declared type. |

Optional record fields are omitted from the binary record when the producer has no value. A reader requires each nonoptional field and constructs optional absence from missing tags. JSON omission and null are projection choices owned by the field definition.
nodes.title: Primitive payloads

nodes.prose: Bytecode, retained host frames and rejected validator context become standard base64. Digests, code-directory hashes, worker identity and fresh-read bytes become lowercase hexadecimal. Path-form fields equal to their input bytes are omitted and listed in `same_as_input`; unavailable forms remain null. Conditional-null fields are carried only when their guard has a value. Other optional fields follow their declared omit/null rule. The generated Rust serializers and independent Python projection apply these rules after typed byte admission.
nodes.title: Public JSON projection

nodes.prose:
The Python retained-byte reader admits captured porcelain frames against the
declared wire schema and projects their fields for the repository's evidence
readers. The received bytes remain with their capture owner.
nodes.title: Retained-byte reader

nodes.prose: The current Rust controls directly cover scalar ranges/booleans/UTF-8, record ID/tag/required-field faults, incomplete prefixes, trailing bytes, fingerprint precedence and shared list/string storage charging. The independently written Python controls additionally exercise variant, map order, impossible count, byte-kind and nesting faults. Equivalent Rust malformed-container controls and a host-writer frame-cap failure observation remain open evidence items.
nodes.title: Primitive reader coverage

nodes.prose: Outcome, state and reason vocabularies travel as text values. Each field's named recipient checks and assessments determine the consequence of a familiar or unfamiliar value. Record references retain their declared record type; equipment references use unsigned indices into their named tables. The declared PWDispositionValue variant has case tag 1 carrying a signed integer and case tag 2 carrying PWRunnerTerminationRequest. Public JSON serializes the selected value directly.

nodes.prose: Each shipped service contains `Contents/MacOS/sb_api_validator`. Direct invocation accepts `[--json] PID [operation filter_type [filter_value]]`; `--batch PID` selects the line protocol above. The leading flags select distinct modes and are not combined.
nodes.title: Direct validator commands

nodes.prose: Direct and batch queries share a filter-name resolver: NONE is 0, PATH is 1, GLOBAL_NAME is 2 and LOCAL_NAME is 3. Conditional SDK names are APPLEEVENT_DESTINATION, RIGHT_NAME, PREFERENCE_DOMAIN, KEXT_BUNDLE_ID, INFO_TYPE, NOTIFICATION_TYPE, XPC_SERVICE_NAME, NVRAM_VARIABLE and POSIX_IPC_NAME when their corresponding sandbox filter macros exist at compilation. `RAW:<number>` uses base-10 strtol, accepts a fully consumed value from 0 through 255 and supplies that numeric filter ID. These accepted helper names are distinct from the host planner’s eligible query pairs.
nodes.title: Choose a native filter

nodes.prose: The direct JSON `denied` Boolean means rc is nonzero, including a native error; it has a broader meaning than batch outcome deny, which requires rc 1 and errno zero. The RAW parser also accepts an empty numeric suffix as zero. Batch’s filter-value grammar treats only the name NONE as valueless, whereas direct mode treats every numeric-zero filter as valueless; a batch RAW:0 value is therefore accepted then unused by the native call. Direct arguments are passed as C strings without batch’s UTF-8 validation. Whether these direct and batch conventions should be aligned remains unresolved.
nodes.title: Direct-mode meaning and input issues

facts.free.condition: An operation and recognized filter are supplied. Numeric filter ID zero requires no filter-value argument; every other ID requires exactly one.
facts.free.effect: Clear errno, invoke sandbox_check for the supplied PID with SANDBOX_CHECK_NO_REPORT, and report the native rc and errno. Plain output is rc=<value> errno=<value> and exits zero for rc zero, one otherwise. JSON mode emits its single-result object and exits zero after the call, whatever its native result.

nodes.prose: CLI filter/argument refusal exits 2. JSON mode emits sb_api_validator_error: bad_filter carries the supplied filter; missing_args, unexpected_filter_value_for_none, missing_filter_value and unexpected_extra_args carry the parsed PID. The native string printer escapes quotes, backslashes and control bytes; remaining argument bytes pass through unchanged.

facts.free.condition: The first positional value is consumed by base-10 strtol and is positive and at most 1,073,741,824, with no trailing bytes.
facts.free.effect: Accept that numeric PID. With no further arguments in direct mode, print ok or the JSON status object and exit zero. With operation arguments, continue to filter admission; batch takes no further positional arguments.

nodes.prose: Before each native call the helper clears errno. Native rc 0 is `allow`; rc 1 with errno 0 is `deny`; rc -1 with EINVAL is `unsupported_operation`; other pairs are `error`. nodes.prose: The batch parser accepts a flat object with exactly the recognized key names; each supplied value is a string. NONE requires filter_value absent; other types require it present. Trailing content, raw NUL, invalid UTF-8, invalid escapes, U+0000 and unpaired surrogates are refused. Standard JSON escapes and paired Unicode surrogate escapes decode to their UTF-8 characters. Physical lines exceeding <!-- span limits.validator_query_payload.value -->65,534<!-- /span --> payload bytes are drained and yield one parse_error diagnostic. Blank lines are skipped. A repeated recognized key currently replaces the earlier parsed value.

nodes.prose: Every admitted object has exact kind, integer schema_version 1, a present string-or-null step_id and nonempty string outcome. Known optional strings and integer fields may be absent or null; Boolean, fractional, string-valued and overflowing numbers cannot supply native integers. Allow/deny require nonempty step_id, operation and filter_type plus integer rc and errno. Every other outcome requires string error. Extra JSON fields and unfamiliar diagnostic outcomes survive in the accepted raw line. Frame size is at most <!-- span limits.validator_reply_frame.value_unit -->8,192 bytes<!-- /span -->; string limits are <!-- span limits.validator_reply_step_id.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> for step_id, <!-- span limits.validator_reply_filter_type.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> for filter_type, <!-- span limits.validator_reply_outcome.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> for outcome, <!-- span limits.validator_reply_operation.value_unit -->127 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> for operation, <!-- span limits.validator_reply_filter_value.value_unit -->1,023 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> for filter_value and <!-- span limits.validator_reply_error.value_unit -->511 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> for error. Rejected context retains at most <!-- span limits.validator_fault_context.value_unit -->256 bytes<!-- /span -->. The validator subprocess account defines this phase collector's total stream and record allowances and subsequent unique-step association.

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

collection and action release, collects worker/validator observations and
produces the host reply. Specimen policy application occurs in the worker so
the host retains its reply path.

shared.prose:
The typed response frame carries a SHA-256 fingerprint of its wire schema.
Its selected schema representation includes record IDs/names, field tags,
names and encoded types, optional and null representation, projections,
variants and roots. The receiver checks this fingerprint before decoding the
producer context for public identity admission. A matching fingerprint
establishes the selected wire-schema match; the public producer identity is
then checked separately.
shared.title: Wire-schema fingerprint

shared.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.

| Value | Host commitment |
| --- | --- |
| `finished` | Execution and required collection completed under the classifier's conditions; each attempt retains its own result. |
| `bad_request` | Reached decoding/admission refused the specimen before worker or validator execution. |
| `bad_policy` | The host could not identify the ordinary source under its structural policy check. |
| `worker_spawn_failed` | The driver could not spawn the worker. |
| `runner_timeout` | Host sentinel or policy-transfer deadline expired, subject to higher-precedence published worker failures. |
| `runner_failed` | Worker preparation/application/publication, host apparatus or supervision failed, or required observations are unusable. |
| `validator_spawn_failed` | Worker classification succeeded and validator spawn failed. |
| `validator_no_reply` | Worker classification succeeded and validator query delivery or verdict reading failed. |
| `validator_decode_failure` | Worker classification succeeded and validator parsing or typed decoding failed. |
| `validator_unavailable` | Required collection was not invoked, its budget/clock failed, or validator supervision/association was unusable. |
| `runner_reporting_failed` | The host failed to validate or encode its assembled report and entered reporting fallback. |

Actor preparation failure selected before scheduler launch. Declarations and
equipment observations from that preparation can remain present.

The host build context. Its public contract string is checked before a
recipient interprets the body.
nodes.title: Producer

nodes.prose:
Zero for `finished`, one for a classified refusal or failure. Native
operations and child exit statuses have separate fields.
nodes.title: Aggregate code

nodes.prose:
Host validation or encoding failure and the fallback's retention state.
Original summary fields are diagnostic values from the rejected report.
nodes.title: Reporting failure

Structured code/path and, when applicable, expected identity for the refusal
selected by the reached decoding or admission branch.
nodes.title: Request refusal

nodes.prose:
Specimen-local token, delivery and handle records with their ownership and
available production/use observations.
nodes.title: Resources

nodes.prose:
The caller's optional label, echoed when available and within admitted bounds.
It labels the experiment and does not select an execution algorithm.
nodes.title: Run label

nodes.prose:
Collected worker supervision, publication and disposition. Absent when no
worker output supplies it; actor subprocess accounts live in actor records.
nodes.title: Ordinary worker

The ordinary driver's observed applied publication when worker output exists.
False leaves application unobserved by this flag; native failure publications
and actor application assessments supply their own evidence. Actor form
omits this top-level flag.

nodes.prose:
Actor scheduling waits, budgets and cancellation. Cancellation is a scheduling
decision, separate from each actor's collected exit evidence.
nodes.title: Schedule

nodes.prose:
The admitted specimen identifier. A JSON-decode refusal uses
`<decode_failed>`; refusal construction sanitizes an unavailable or
over-capacity identifier.
nodes.title: Specimen identifier

nodes.prose:
Probe rows in declared action order, with query, attempt and comparison
observations. Refusals before worker execution and the minimal reporting
fallback use an empty array.
nodes.title: Probe results

nodes.prose:
Accepted instrumentation echoed by orchestration, with refusal sanitation
where required. It identifies the selected execution configuration.
nodes.title: Instrumentation

nodes.prose: Host observations of extension delivery attempts and recipient acknowledgements.
nodes.title: Transfers

shared.prose: The capture sequence belongs to the actor whose activation was stored. Time may be unavailable while the store and ordinal remain observed.
shared.title: Host activation observation
