shared.title: capture_ordinal

shared.prose: Host monotonic time in nanoseconds after the store, when the clock supplied it.
shared.title: observed_ns

shared.prose: The host emits actors in request order. Each actor owns its launch, worker publications, policy receipt, equipment read-back and lifecycle account.
shared.title: Actor process account

facts.free.condition: Assemble each actor's row from its declaration, launch/driver output and its own shared publications; phases retain their declared actor and action ownership.
facts.free.effect: Retain the actor-indexed account and separately report schedule observations. In an ordinary executed reply, each declared action has its ordered step or extension-event record even when execution evidence is unresolved. Preparation refusals and retained reporting failures carry the distinct contents stated below.

shared.prose:
A preparation refusal retains declarations and preparation observations while
its execution tables remain empty. A retained reporting-failure reply carries
the assembled observations and the reporting conflict, with comparison claims
removed. Its applicable guarantee is the degraded report's form: retained
actor, phase and resource associations remain available for inspection as
assembled. Ordinary consistency assessments apply on the ordinary reply path.
shared.title: Actor ownership and reporting scope

shared.prose: Submitted actor identifier that binds this row to its phases and resources.
shared.title: actor_id

shared.prose: Host application-boundary assessment with its evidence basis.
shared.title: application

shared.prose: Zero or one from the final acquired applied publication, retained even when a setup deadline already ended eligibility.
shared.title: application_count

shared.prose: Acquired worker applied flag for apply mode when output exists; absent for an unapplied declaration or unavailable output.
shared.title: applied

shared.prose: Receipt from this actor's requested compiled-profile capture, when the host has a capture result.
shared.title: compiled_profile

shared.prose: Requested and resolved worker role, entitlement requirement assessment and live execution observation.
shared.title: equipment

shared.prose: Zero-based position in the admitted actor list.
shared.title: index

shared.prose: Host-arranged launch context once this actor process was spawned.
shared.title: launch

shared.prose: Submitted sandbox mode, apply or unapplied.
shared.title: mode

shared.prose: Host-owned waitpid ending retained for this actor and referenced by dependent termination gates.
shared.title: owned_reap

shared.prose: Selected policy representation for an apply actor, when provided.
shared.title: policy_format

shared.prose: Worker SHA-256 of the bytes it actually read before compilation, when published.
shared.title: policy_received_sha256

shared.prose: Host SHA-256 of the selected submitted source bytes after controller augmentation.
shared.title: policy_sha256

shared.prose:
The host and controller apply actor/equipment/gate assessment on the ordinary
reporting path. The Python lifecycle receipt reader checks those predicates
for actor-form reporting-failure replies too. The general JSON consumer skips
its extension checks there but still checks actor identities, launch and
phase/step associations. Its preparation partition exception requires a valid
preparation-failure shape. The degraded form guarantee and preservation of
assembled observations above govern retained reporting failures. These reader
scopes still need reconciliation and a common corpus; a gate-specific
disagreement remains an unestablished case.
shared.title: Reader scope requiring reconciliation

shared.prose: Host setup classification: not_launched, launch_refused, transfer_failed, applied, unapplied_declared, setup_failed, authority_setup_failed, exited_before_setup or setup_timeout.
shared.title: setup_status

shared.prose: This actor's worker lifecycle and publication account.
shared.title: subprocess

shared.prose: One-based global phase ordinals declared for this actor, including visits whose activation never occurred.
shared.title: visits

shared.prose: The host classifies the apply-call boundary from mode, launch, applied publication, eligible authority failure and terminal worker evidence, in that precedence order.
shared.title: Application assessment

shared.prose: The specific declaration, launch state or worker/authority publication supporting state. The eleven permitted state/basis pairs are defined by the application rule below.
shared.title: basis

facts.free.condition: Evaluate the following branches in displayed precedence order. A terminal worker branch requires failure_state published and the specified operation/code/native-kind combination.
facts.free.effect: Publish exactly the state/basis pair of the first matching branch.

shared.prose: The worker's applied publication is true.
shared.title: Applied flag

shared.prose: Terminal operation 8, code 1, native kind 1 has a nonzero native result.
shared.title: Native apply failure

shared.prose:
An observed authority decision is `terminal_required_failure` and carries no
setup integrity error.
shared.title: Authority refusal

shared.prose: Progress identifies operation 8 and stage 1 or 2, after all earlier branches failed.
shared.title: Apply boundary without result

shared.prose: Terminal operation 5/code 1/native kind 2.
shared.title: Compile refusal

shared.prose:
Terminal operation 1 has code 4, 7, 10 or 12 and native kind 0; or operation 2
has code 2, 3, 9 or 13.
shared.title: Input refusal

shared.prose:
Terminal operation 1/code 5/kind 0; operation 3/code 1/kind 2; or operation 4
with code 1/kind 1 or code 6/kind 0.
shared.title: Parameter refusal

shared.prose: The preceding evidence branches did not establish another pair.
shared.title: Remaining evidence

shared.prose: Terminal operation 12 has code 1/kind 1, code 14/kind 0, or code 15/detail 1/kind 0.
shared.title: Timing refusal

shared.prose: Mode is `unapplied`.
shared.title: Unapplied declaration

shared.prose: Apply mode has no launched worker.
shared.title: Worker absent

shared.prose:
Final actor collection preserves a later applied publication and derives
`application_count` from it even after setup eligibility ended. The exact
combination of `setup_timeout` with an observed applied publication still
needs an owning behavioral check; the current account is supported by source.
shared.title: Setup deadline and later application

shared.prose: not_requested, not_attempted, observed or unobserved. observed identifies evidence of the apply boundary, including a native apply failure; unobserved retains an unresolved result.
shared.title: state

shared.prose: The gate belongs to the dependent phase and observes the named source actor after that source’s final scheduled visit was activated.
shared.title: Termination dependency

shared.prose: True exactly for a satisfied gate, allowing this dependent phase to proceed to activation.
shared.title: activation_eligible

shared.prose:
The scheduler source cancels every phase after a failed evaluated gate. The
read timeout check covers the dependent phase; a focused check still needs
to assert an additional later phase owned by another actor and its public
cancellation account.
shared.title: Cancellation-scope evidence

shared.prose: Capture of the gate result in the source child's host-observation sequence; absent for not_reached and when no source session supplies a sequence.
shared.title: capture_ordinal

facts.free.condition: Resolve source and final-phase joins before using s or f; missing, nonfinal, same-actor or nonpreceding associations are findings. Check owned PID/native-status agreement, all conditional gate captures, independent actor setup/equipment eligibility and activation timing.
facts.free.effect: Add actor_evidence issues for failed requirements; set top-level disposition_integrity invalid, process_disposition withheld and termination_cause unknown. Preserve the host reply, each actor's independently projected disposition, run result and exit status.

facts.free.condition: True eligibility also requires the dependent actor's applied or unapplied_declared setup and eligible equipment. False eligibility requires absent activation/visit timing, false arrival/proceed flags and collection not_reached.

shared.prose:
Gate findings carry `actor_evidence` and a detail sentence. They currently
lack a structured actor or phase reference joining the issue to its gate.
The host's gate fields remain present beside the controller's overall finding.
shared.title: Finding subject

shared.prose:
The referenced ending matches the source actor's valid PID/native wait status,
has stage `schedule` or `termination_gate`, and has the reference's positive
ordinal. Final activation and reap timestamps must exist in nondecreasing
order; a timestamped dependent activation is at or after the reap.
shared.title: Source sequence

shared.prose:
Every present gate wait has budget 0–5000 and absent excluded time. An
evaluated gate has a wait whose stop matches its outcome.
shared.title: Timely satisfied wait

shared.prose: An unreached gate carries its declaration and false eligibility.
shared.title: Unreached shape

shared.prose: terminated, the supported dependency condition.
shared.title: condition

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

facts.free.condition: Evaluate only after the schedule remains uncancelled, its allowance is positive, and the dependent actor session, usable setup, unstopped state and visit are available. Evaluation first checks the source session and final declared phase activation; unavailable source evidence gives source_unavailable.
facts.free.effect: Set activation_eligible from satisfied. A failed evaluated gate prevents dependent activation, collection and release, and cancels every later scheduled phase regardless of its actor. Cleanup and final collection continue for launched actors.
facts.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

shared.prose:
The dependency wait observes the owned source child without requesting its
departure. Its budget is the lesser of <!-- span limits.actor_termination_wait.value_unit -->5,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> and the remaining
execution allowance in whole milliseconds. Deadline samples and final elapsed
accounting govern satisfaction. These are charged-wait conditions; operating
system scheduling determines when the host next runs.

A failed evaluated gate sets `schedule.cancelled` to
`termination_dependency:<outcome>`. Later phases retain their declarations
with collection `not_reached`, false arrival/completion and absent activation
and visit timing. Their own gates remain `not_reached`. Final cleanup may add
the source's later owned ending while the failed gate keeps the observation
reference captured during its evaluation.
shared.title: Evaluating and applying the dependency

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

shared.prose:
A deadline sample, required activation/reap time or final elapsed accounting
was unavailable or moved backward. Retained fields provide the available
context for this timing failure.
shared.title: Timing unavailable

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

shared.prose:
Evaluation began with no positive whole-millisecond gate budget. A schedule
allowance check that stops traversal earlier leaves the gate `not_reached`.
shared.title: No remaining gate allowance

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

shared.prose:
Cancellation, exhausted schedule allowance or an unavailable dependent actor
or visit stopped traversal before this gate was evaluated. Its wait,
observation and capture ordinal are absent and eligibility is false. An
unavailable dependent actor can leave this gate unreached while later
otherwise eligible phases remain schedulable.
shared.title: Unreached

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

shared.prose: The host's uninterrupted source ownership was lost or its source wait failed.
shared.title: Ownership lost

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

facts.free.condition: The source final activation precedes a natural owned reap in its child sequence; both timestamps exist and activation time is at most reap time. Ownership is unbroken, departure_requested is false, budget is positive, deadline samples permit the reap, and final wait has a valid elapsed interval at most budget.

shared.prose:
The gate closes after the source's owned ending. A normal exit or signaled
ending can qualify; natural means the host had not requested departure.
Source final-phase completion is a separate observation from activation and
owned termination.
shared.title: Satisfied

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

shared.prose: The host had requested the source's departure before the eligible ending.
shared.title: Departure requested

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

shared.prose:
The source session, final activation, or required activation-before-ending
order was unavailable.
shared.title: Source unavailable

context.where: serial actor schedule before dependent activation

shared.prose:
The deadline or wait expired, including after a reap, or final elapsed time
exceeded budget. A retained reap reference establishes that capture while
this outcome records failure to establish timely satisfaction.
shared.title: Gate timeout

shared.prose: Reference to the source actor's owned ending captured by the evaluated gate, when available; a late ending can remain beside a failed gate.
shared.title: observation

shared.prose: not_reached, satisfied, timed_out, ownership_lost, clock_unavailable, source_unavailable, source_departure_requested or execution_allowance_exhausted; each is defined by the gate rule below.
shared.title: outcome

shared.prose: Different actor named by the dependent phase's after_termination declaration.
shared.title: source_actor_id

shared.prose: Source actor's last declared phase, which must precede the dependent phase in the global schedule.
shared.title: source_final_phase_id

shared.prose:
The source completes its final phase but remains alive when the dependency
times out. The dependent phase receives no activation, collection or release.
Cleanup later reaps the source; the gate remains `timed_out`.
shared.title: A timeout followed by cleanup

shared.prose: Host dependency wait, with budget capped at <!-- span limits.actor_termination_wait.value_unit -->5,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> and charged to remaining execution allowance. Absent for not_reached.
shared.title: wait

shared.prose: The host starts each actor as a fresh process with explicit standard streams and descriptor inheritance.
shared.title: Actor launch context

shared.prose: empty: the host supplies an empty environment to the actor process.
shared.title: environment

shared.prose: Explicit inherited descriptor numbers: 0 policy input, 3 shared evidence, 4 readiness, and 5 only when an authority region is mapped for the actor.
shared.title: inherited_descriptors

shared.prose: PID of the runner host that spawned the actor.
shared.title: parent_pid

shared.prose: PID obtained from this actor's successful spawn.
shared.title: pid

shared.prose: stdin_policy_pipe_stdout_stderr_null_device: stdin carries policy bytes, while stdout and stderr are attached to the null device.
shared.title: standard_streams

shared.prose: The host reports phases in declared schedule order. Observation fields record activation's consequences separately from the declared phase and action identities.
shared.title: Phase collection and execution

shared.prose: Declared action identifiers in phase order, retained even when actions produce no execution observations.
shared.title: action_ids

shared.prose: Host release-store observation which activates this phase, with its actor-local capture ordinal and optional time.
shared.title: activation_observation

shared.prose: Actor owning this phase in actor form; absent for the single-worker form.
shared.title: actor_id

shared.prose: One-based visit number within this actor's declared visits, distinct from global ordinal.
shared.title: actor_visit

shared.prose: Whether the host acquired the active worker's arrival publication for this visit.
shared.title: arrival_observed

shared.prose: collected, not_needed, budget_exhausted, clock_unavailable or not_reached. collected identifies an invoked collection even when validator I/O or decoding later fails.
shared.title: collection_status

shared.prose: Whether the host acquired completion for this visit.
shared.title: completion_observed

shared.prose: Collection/release order observations for this phase, including host proceed store and worker acknowledgement.
shared.title: ordering

shared.prose: One-based position in the global phase schedule.
shared.title: ordinal

shared.prose: Submitted phase identifier used by its action records and validator collection.
shared.title: phase_id

shared.prose: Dependency observation for a phase declaring after_termination, including gates left not_reached.
shared.title: termination_gate

shared.prose: Native validator spawn failure before a validator child existed.
shared.title: validator_spawn_failure

shared.prose: Child-process and accepted-verdict account for this phase's validator collection.
shared.title: validator_subprocess

shared.prose: Host-measured intervals for reached visit boundaries; missing intervals retain unavailable clock/boundary observations.
shared.title: visit_timing

shared.prose: The schedule records aggregate allowances and cancellation alongside individual actor and phase facts.
shared.title: Schedule account

shared.prose: Recorded schedule cancellation reason, such as preparation_refused, execution_allowance_exhausted, an equipment failure or termination_dependency followed by its outcome; absent when no cancellation was recorded.
shared.title: cancelled

shared.prose: Recorded production maximum for aggregate query collection across actor phases: <!-- span limits.actor_collection_allowance.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The host reports this maximum even when `_test_overrides.validator_total_timeout_ms` reduces the allowance used for collection.
shared.title: collection_budget_ms

shared.prose: Measured schedule traversal wait, with collection excluded when separately budgeted.
shared.title: execution_wait

shared.prose: Overall actor-run lifetime allowance, <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> in the production plan.
shared.title: lifetime_budget_ms

shared.prose: Measured shared setup wait for the actor set.
shared.title: setup_wait

shared.prose: Each interval measures two host observations in milliseconds; an unavailable or backward clock leaves that interval absent.
shared.title: Visit intervals

shared.prose: Time between the host activation store and acquired worker arrival.
shared.title: activation_to_arrival_ms

shared.prose: Time from observed arrival to the host proceed release store.
shared.title: arrival_to_release_ms

shared.prose: Time spent in the phase's synchronous query-collection hook.
shared.title: collection_ms

shared.prose: Time from the release store to acquired worker completion.
shared.title: release_to_completion_ms

shared.prose: An action is one JSON object in the phase actions array. The decoder chooses an extension action when the `extension` key is present; otherwise it decodes a paired probe. A present null extension therefore selects extension decoding and fails its required object.
shared.title: Phase action variants

shared.prose: The ordinary and actor forms currently differ on empty step IDs. Aligning them requires an explicit admission decision; this draft preserves the implemented distinction.
shared.title: Empty ordinary identifiers

shared.prose: The extension variant is `PWRunnerExtensionAction`: a step ID and closed extension operation, as defined by the extensions surface. It contributes no sandbox query.
shared.title: Extension action

facts.free.effect: Refuse repeated step IDs across the complete specimen. Actor actions require nonempty IDs. The ordinary form currently accepts an empty step ID when it is unique.

shared.prose: The probe variant is `PWRunnerProbeStep`: a step ID, sandbox query and attempt, as defined by the probes surface.
shared.title: Paired probe

shared.prose: A specimen admits at most <!-- span limits.actors.value_unit -->8 items<!-- /span -->. Each actor has at least one declared phase. Each required-entitlement list fits <!-- span limits.actor_required_entitlements.value_unit -->64 items<!-- /span -->, with each key bounded by <!-- span limits.actor_entitlement_key.value_unit -->255 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->.
shared.title: Actor declaration

shared.prose: Nonempty specimen-local actor identifier, unique across actors and bounded by <!-- span limits.actor_id.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->. Native transport also requires NUL-free bytes.
shared.title: actor_id

shared.prose: Equipment role: `selected` uses the selected runner worker; `unentitled` uses the packaged unentitled worker. Omission selects `selected`; present null is refused.
shared.title: equipment

facts.free.effect: Launch one fresh worker for each actor. An apply worker compiles and applies its own declared policy once before its visits; an unapplied worker publishes that declaration and executes under the restrictions already inherited by its process. Keep that worker for its successive visits.

Require unique nonempty actor IDs, known equipment roles, valid sandbox declarations, valid entitlement demands, and at least one phase per actor. Build one resolved plan whose actor and resource indexes govern execution.

shared.prose: Static and live read-back demand for boolean-true entitlement keys on this actor's executable. Omission supplies an empty list; present null is refused. Keys must be nonempty and unique.
shared.title: required_entitlements

shared.prose: The actor's explicit apply or unapplied declaration; application assessment is reported separately from this request.
shared.title: sandbox

shared.prose: The declaration names a source actor, while the gate reports the host's owned observation of its ending.
shared.title: Termination dependency

shared.prose: Known actor whose final declared phase occurs earlier than the dependent phase. It must differ from the dependent phase's actor.
shared.title: actor_id

facts.free.effect: At admission require the source's final declared visit before the dependent phase. Before activating the dependent actor or collecting its predictions, evaluate the owned natural-reap gate. A failed evaluated gate cancels every remaining scheduled phase.

shared.prose: The actor form admits <!-- span limits.actor_phases.value_unit -->16 items<!-- /span --> and the ordinary form <!-- span limits.phase_count.value_unit -->8 items<!-- /span -->. Across either form, actions share the <!-- span limits.probe_steps.value_unit -->256 items<!-- /span --> total capacity.
shared.title: Phase declaration

shared.prose: Actions in declaration order, including an empty array. Ordinary phases contain paired probes. Actor phases may also contain extension actions. Action identifiers are unique across the whole specimen.
shared.title: actions

shared.prose: Required known actor owner in the actor form. The ordinary form requires absence or null.
shared.title: actor_id

shared.prose: Optional owned-termination dependency in the actor form. Absence supplies no dependency; present null is refused. The ordinary form refuses a supplied dependency.
shared.title: after_termination

shared.prose: The phase-order source has been inspected in the wider examination. Integrated order-barrier and mutation controls must be attached to the completed release account; this draft credits no execution of those controls.
shared.title: Barrier execution evidence

facts.free.effect: Close the active phase's eligible prediction collection before releasing its actions; run those actions in declaration order. Begin the next phase's collection after the previous phase completes. In the actor form activate one actor at a time while other workers remain parked.

shared.prose: Nonempty identifier unique across the specimen's phases and bounded by <!-- span limits.phase_id.value_unit -->63 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and NUL-free.
shared.title: phase_id

shared.prose: `apply` requires a policy and asks the worker to compile/apply it; `unapplied` requires policy absence or null and records the inherited process restrictions as its starting condition.
shared.title: mode

shared.prose: Required non-null policy for `apply`; a non-null policy is refused for `unapplied`. Each apply policy has its own source, parameters, augmentation and capture request.
shared.title: policy

shared.prose: Selection resolves the actor’s role, binds its entitlement requirements and carries the live inspection result used for activation eligibility.
shared.title: Actor equipment selection

shared.prose: Zero-based index of the selected role/source row in equipment_bindings once that row exists.
shared.title: binding_ref

shared.prose: Live code and entitlement observation for the owned actor process before activation.
shared.title: execution

shared.prose: Requested keys whose values are absent or are not Boolean true, in request order. Empty means all satisfied; absence accompanies unobserved.
shared.title: missing_requirements

shared.prose: Explicit selected or unentitled request; null when the request omitted equipment.
shared.title: requested

shared.prose: Distinct requested entitlement keys, at most <!-- span limits.actor_required_entitlements.value -->64<!-- /span -->; each nonempty key is at most <!-- span limits.actor_entitlement_key.value_unit -->255 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->.
shared.title: required_entitlements

shared.prose: satisfied or unsatisfied from the static entitlement dictionary; unobserved when read-back is unavailable.
shared.title: requirements_status

shared.prose: Requested role, defaulting to selected when omitted.
shared.title: resolved

shared.prose: The host separates run prerequisites, actor shared regions and token custody into their owning scopes.
shared.title: Host authority scopes

shared.prose: Per-token host-private custody allocation, erasure and unmap observations.
shared.title: custody

shared.prose: Per-actor shared authority-region allocation, initialization, descriptor and cleanup observations.
shared.title: regions

shared.prose: Run-wide prerequisite account, including core-limit setup.
shared.title: run

shared.prose: Each fixed slot identifies one operation once. Kind controls which native fields are meaningful; cleanup cells retain their own failures alongside the primary setup failure.
shared.title: Authority operation cell

shared.prose: Operation-specific validation reason, including descriptor_missing or header magic/identity/actor_index/slot_counts/region_extent mismatch.
shared.title: detail

shared.prose: Captured native errno on failed integer/mapping operations; absent for other states and kinds.
shared.title: errno

shared.prose: integer, error_code, mapping, symbol, validation or memory, identifying the observation convention.
shared.title: native_kind

shared.prose: Recorded return for integer/error_code operations; absent for mapping, symbol, validation and memory observations.
shared.title: native_rc

shared.prose: Operation registered for that scope and slot, such as descriptor_close, header_binding, shm_unlink or final_erase.
shared.title: operation

shared.prose: setup or cleanup, according to the operation's boundary.
shared.title: role

shared.prose: Zero-based fixed operation-cell position within its worker, region, custody or run scope.
shared.title: slot

shared.prose:
The index within each list is its fixed slot. Worker descriptor close can
belong to setup or cleanup according to the branch. Worker slots 11–12,
region slots 8–11 and custody slots 1–2 are cleanup. Integer/error-code
operations publish their return; failed integer/mapping operations publish
errno. Symbol, validation and memory states carry their corresponding
observation without an invented integer return.
shared.title: Registered operation slots

shared.prose: succeeded/failed for native integer or mapping operations; accepted/rejected for validation; available/unavailable for symbols; performed for memory operations; not_attempted for an explicitly unattempted cell.
shared.title: state

shared.prose: Operation-specific unsigned native observation when the cell marks a value present, such as object/page size.
shared.title: value

shared.prose: A scope retains operation cells, its setup decision and ownership state. A decision and individual operation publications have separate acquisition boundaries.
shared.title: Authority operation scope

facts.free.condition: After worker-identity agreement, acquire-load the decision snapshot first, then independently acquire-load each published operation cell.
facts.free.effect: Retain valid cells even when the decision is absent. For an observed decision, validate its actor/required association and primary failed/rejected cell, recording setup_primary_unpublished when that supporting cell is unavailable.

shared.prose:
The decision's release orders prerequisite cells. Reading the decision first
keeps a newly observed decision joined to its earlier primary publication.
Each cell still has its own publication flag and kind/state guards. A cleanup
cell can therefore be retained before the terminal decision appears. Invalid
cells contribute integrity errors while independently valid observations
remain available.
shared.title: Acquiring setup decisions and operations

shared.prose: Bound actor identifier for worker or region scope, when applicable.
shared.title: actor_id

shared.prose: Zero-based actor position for worker or region scope.
shared.title: actor_index

shared.prose: Retained unresolved shared-memory name after successful creation and failed unlink, requiring ownership-aware recovery.
shared.title: cleanup_reference

shared.prose: Worker decision ready, not_required or terminal_required_failure when observed; host scope state such as not_attempted, ready or failed records its own preparation.
shared.title: disposition

shared.prose: Detected malformed, repeated, missing-primary or mismatched-association publications; absence means the decoder found none.
shared.title: integrity_errors

shared.prose: Independently observed operation cells in slot order, including cleanup after a setup failure.
shared.title: operations

shared.prose: Named ownership states: object_name, descriptor and mapping use not_acquired, held, released or unresolved; shared_erasure/private_erasure use not_present, performed, withheld_not_quiescent or unobserved.
shared.title: ownership

shared.prose: Slot of the first failed/rejected operation supporting the scope decision; worker terminal_required_failure requires that published primary cell.
shared.title: primary_operation

shared.prose: Worker decision acquisition: observed or not_observed; host-recorded scopes use their directly recorded disposition.
shared.title: publication

shared.prose: Whether authority setup is required for the worker's admitted actor plan.
shared.title: required

shared.prose: Zero-based token position for custody scope.
shared.title: token_index

shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.
shared.title: Associating the owned process

shared.prose:
| Operation | Required operands | Producing actor and consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue` | `family`, `target`, `authority`, `token_ref` | Active actor calls native file issuance once with class selected by authority, exact target and flags zero; assigns the declared token resource. |
| `transfer` | `token_ref`, `recipient`, `delivery_ref` | Token-owning actor publishes a host request for one assigned recipient slot; assigns the delivery resource. |
| `consume` | `delivery_ref`, `handle_ref` | Recipient actor calls native consume on its usable delivered token; assigns the handle resource. |
| `release` | `handle_ref` | Consuming actor calls native release for its candidate handle. |

Each other operand must be absent. A required null operand is missing for this grammar; an extraneous null operand is inapplicable.

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
Every controller and compiler-helper envelope carries these string fields
under `build`. They identify the emitting binary's compiled context.
shared.title: Build identification

shared.prose:
The Git HEAD object name observed by the packaged build, or `unknown` when
unavailable. Direct Rust compilation reads `PW_BUILD_COMMIT` with an absent
value falling back to `unknown`. Describe and commit report provenance;
identity admission compares the contract field.
shared.title: Commit

shared.prose:
The descriptive source coordinate compiled into the producer. `build.sh`
uses `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty`, falling back
to `unknown`. Direct Rust compilation reads `PW_BUILD_DESCRIBE` with an absent
value falling back to `unknown`.
shared.title: Describe

shared.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
shared.title: Absent field

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
shared.title: Effect

shared.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
shared.title: Null value

shared.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
shared.title: Observation

shared.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
shared.title: Phase

shared.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
shared.title: Prediction

shared.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
shared.title: Request

shared.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
shared.title: Specimen

shared.title: Describe

shared.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.
shared.title: Exact admission identity

shared.prose:
The Rust controller and compiler helper embed a nonempty compile-time
`PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` verbatim. An absent or empty value becomes `unbound`.
Ordinary SwiftPM compilation uses `unbound`; its explicitly selected unit-test
context uses `test:policy-witness`. Rust unit tests likewise use
`test:policy-witness`. A request cannot pass the controller's identity gate
when its expected identity is empty or `unbound`.
shared.title: Direct compilation contexts

shared.prose:
The direct Rust environment path is established by the compile-time constant
and Cargo's environment tracking. The available plain-Cargo integration check
removes `PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` and establishes the unbound case. A direct Cargo
build with an explicitly supplied foreign or release-form identity has not
been exercised in this examination.
shared.title: Direct-build evidence limit

shared.prose:
`release:vX.Y.Z` names the sole annotated release tag at the build checkout's
HEAD. The build derives this form when the checkout is clean, the tag matches
`v<digits>.<digits>.<digits>`, and the selected files' actual bytes and inventory
equal that tag's blobs. More than one qualifying annotated tag on a clean
HEAD refuses identity derivation as ambiguous.

`development:<sha256>` identifies the selected source paths and bytes in
other source trees. Its digest is SHA-256 with the domain prefix
`PolicyWitness public build contract` followed by a NUL byte. For each sorted
repository-relative path, the generator appends the UTF-8 path and file bytes,
each preceded by its unsigned eight-byte big-endian length. A dirty release
checkout receives this development form. A documentation-only edit can change
the form from release to development while leaving the selected-source digest
unchanged.
shared.title: Release and development forms

facts.free.condition: Resolve each question from the owning worker's acquired output, unique slot identities and submitted plan. A not_reached or unpublished conclusion requires terminal collection where specified below.

facts.where: final worker output and plan join

shared.prose:
An exit code or signal is supported after a successful reap. Both representations
produce a D1 conflict. A completed supported slot establishes publication and
can establish entry. Recognized progress at or after an attempt's entry also
establishes entry. A final earlier progress position establishes `not_reached`
only after confirmed reaping and with an incomplete slot; beside a completed
slot it produces D5. Returned-or-later terminal progress beside an incomplete
supported slot produces D5 for result publication. Live collection leaves
missing results unresolved. An unsupported attempt has inapplicable result
publication and an `unsupported` lifecycle summary.
shared.title: Resolving lifecycle claims

shared.prose: Plan-ordered lifecycle claims for each requested step, joined only to uniquely identified worker slots.

shared.prose:
The host binds each validator collection to its phase and retains accepted records through later I/O, association or cleanup failure.

For N submitted queries, the collector assigns a record allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_records_per_query.value -->2<!-- /span --> and a stdout retention allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_reply_bytes_per_query.value_unit -->16,384 bytes<!-- /span -->. The allowances are sized before writing the query batch. On byte overflow the host counts all bytes received, keeps the bounded prefix through its last complete LF frame, closes collection and reports byte_limit. Decoding retains complete accepted records before the first refused frame or record-count excess.
shared.title: Validator subprocess

facts.free.condition: Join each expected ID to exactly one accepted record whose supplied query metadata agrees; allow/deny additionally require the complete submitted query identity.
facts.free.effect: Exclude ambiguous, missing or mismatched records from the per-step join, retain every accepted record in the collection and publish association_issues.

remain unassociated. Diagnostic outcomes may omit query metadata; any supplied
metadata must agree. A decoding fault retains the accepted prefix and the
rejected frame's bounded byte context. Transport or later cleanup failure
preserves the already accepted observations.

```scheme
(version 1)
(deny default)
(allow file-read* (literal (string-append (param "ROOT") "/hosts")))
```

shared.prose: A successful spawn supplies a child PID even if the child later exits nonzero. The child collection, termination request and owned reap remain separate observations. The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.

shared.prose:
The worker runs the selected operation after policy application in an apply worker, or after the unapplied actor's setup:

| Kind / action | Native operation and operation-specific consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `file / open_read` | `open(O_RDONLY)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte read and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; read and close results are discarded. |
| `file / open_write` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_TRUNC)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte `x` write and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; write and close results are discarded. |
| `file / create` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CREAT, 0600)` then close. Creation mode is subject to umask. An existing file is opened without truncation or exclusive creation. |
| `file / read_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_RDONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)`, `fstat`, one read bounded by <!-- span limits.fresh_read_bytes.value_unit -->64 bytes<!-- /span -->, then close. Record each boundary and read bytes; aggregate failure selects stat, read or close failure after a successful open. |
| `file / write_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)` of an existing target, opened `fstat`, `ftruncate(0)`, truncated `fstat`, one-byte `x` write after successful truncation, written `fstat`, then close. Preserve the first failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / create_fresh` | `lstat` before a fresh exclusive `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC \| O_CREAT \| O_EXCL, 0600)`, opened `fstat`, one-byte `x` write, written `fstat`, then close. Pre-open `lstat` is an independent observation. Preserve the first operation failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / unlink` | `unlink(target)` and its return/errno. |
| `file / access` | `access(target, R_OK)` and its return/errno. This is an access-check observation. |
| `mach / lookup` | Obtain the task bootstrap port and call `bootstrap_look_up` for the supplied name; release the returned service port on success. |
| `sysctl / read` | One `sysctlbyname` call with a <!-- span limits.sysctl_read_bytes.value_unit -->4,096 bytes<!-- /span --> buffer acquired after application. Report the call's result and errno; discard value bytes and the returned length. |
| `exec / spawn` | Prepare per-attempt child resources, call `posix_spawn` for the absolute target with the requested argv, then collect child and cleanup observations. |

A short fresh write records its native count and fails the aggregate while retaining zero native errno when the write returned a short nonnegative count. A fresh file descriptor belongs to that attempt and is closed before its result is published.

nodes.prose:
`read_fresh` performs descriptor stat, bounded read and close after a
successful open. The first stat, read or close failure supplies the
aggregate failure. A successful read records the bytes actually returned.

`write_fresh` opens, records descriptor metadata, truncates to zero,
records metadata again, writes one byte if truncation succeeded, records
metadata after that write and closes. `create_fresh` first records a
path-stat diagnostic, then opens with exclusive creation, records descriptor
metadata, writes one byte, records metadata and closes. Creation's pre-open
stat is diagnostic. Metadata, truncate, write and close failures preserve
the first failed descriptor operation; a short write fails with its
observed count. Unreached operations remain absent.

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
The XPC host admits the request, prepares worker resources, coordinates query
collection and action release, collects worker/validator observations and
produces the host reply. Specimen policy application occurs in the worker so
the host retains its reply path.

facts.free.effect: After application or an actor's unapplied declaration, acquire stdout/stderr pipes and spawn actions for this released attempt, release them on setup failure and at completion, and report the failing setup call when spawning was prevented. Spawn with target as argv[0], an empty environment, /dev/null stdin, captured stdout/stderr, close-on-exec descriptor policy and a new process group.

shared.prose: A successful spawn supplies a child PID even if the child later exits nonzero. The child collection, termination request and owned reap remain separate observations. The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.
shared.title: Exec setup and child inputs

nodes.prose:
An exit code or signal is supported after a successful reap. Both representations
produce a D1 conflict. A completed supported slot establishes publication and
can establish entry. Recognized progress at or after an attempt's entry also
establishes entry. A final earlier progress position establishes `not_reached`
only after confirmed reaping and with an incomplete slot; beside a completed
slot it produces D5. Returned-or-later terminal progress beside an incomplete
supported slot produces D5 for result publication. Live collection leaves
missing results unresolved. An unsupported attempt has inapplicable result
publication and an `unsupported` lifecycle summary.

nodes.prose:
The host binds each validator collection to its phase and retains accepted records through later I/O, association or cleanup failure.

For N submitted queries, the collector assigns a record allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_records_per_query.value -->2<!-- /span --> and a stdout retention allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_reply_bytes_per_query.value_unit -->16,384 bytes<!-- /span -->. The allowances are sized before writing the query batch. On byte overflow the host counts all bytes received, keeps the bounded prefix through its last complete LF frame, closes collection and reports byte_limit. Decoding retains complete accepted records before the first refused frame or record-count excess.

shared.prose: A successful spawn supplies a child PID even if the child later exits nonzero. The child collection, termination request and owned reap remain separate observations. The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.

nodes.prose:
The dependency wait observes the owned source child without requesting its
departure. Its budget is the lesser of <!-- span limits.actor_termination_wait.value_unit -->5,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> and the remaining
execution allowance in whole milliseconds. Deadline samples and final elapsed
accounting govern satisfaction. These are charged-wait conditions; operating
system scheduling determines when the host next runs.

A failed evaluated gate sets `schedule.cancelled` to
`termination_dependency:<outcome>`. Later phases retain their declarations
with collection `not_reached`, false arrival/completion and absent activation
and visit timing. Their own gates remain `not_reached`. Final cleanup may add
the source's later owned ending while the failed gate keeps the observation
reference captured during its evaluation.

Mismatch or inspection failure cancels all scheduling, retains earlier setup/application publications and leaves all phases unactivated and uncollected. An unavailable setup can coexist with other usable actors when no inspection failure cancels them.

shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.
shared.title: Associating the owned process

shared.prose:
The host binds each validator collection to its phase and retains accepted records through later I/O, association or cleanup failure.

For N submitted queries, the collector assigns a record allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_records_per_query.value -->2<!-- /span --> and a stdout retention allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_reply_bytes_per_query.value_unit -->16,384 bytes<!-- /span -->. The allowances are sized before writing the query batch. On byte overflow the host counts all bytes received, keeps the bounded prefix through its last complete LF frame, closes collection and reports byte_limit. Decoding retains complete accepted records before the first refused frame or record-count excess.

errno. Symbol, validation and memory states carry their corresponding
observation without an invented integer return.

The decision's release orders prerequisite cells. Reading the decision first
keeps a newly observed decision joined to its earlier primary publication.
Each cell still has its own publication flag and kind/state guards. A cleanup
cell can therefore be retained before the terminal decision appears. Invalid
cells contribute integrity errors while independently valid observations
remain available.

nodes.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.

nodes.prose:
| Value or boundary | Result and retained account |
| --- | --- |
| `bad_request` | Decoded request admission refused; exit 1, structured refusal when supplied, dossier retained. |
| `tool_error` | CLI/input/configuration, client launch or request delivery failed; exit 2. A returned client capture remains on delivery refusal. |
| `missing_runner_client` | No retained client capture; exit 1. |
| `unsupported_runner_client` | Client producer/schema admission failed; exit 1, bounded rejected bytes retained. |
| `malformed_runner_client` | Client frame or capture semantics failed; exit 1, bounded rejected bytes retained. |
| `runner_reply_truncated` | Accepted capture says host bytes were truncated; exit 1, prefix retained. |
| `unsupported_runner_response` | Host schema/public identity failed; exit 1, captured bytes retained. |
| `malformed_runner_response` | Host decoding, capacity or label check failed; exit 1. A structurally decoded report remains when the later gate refused it. |
| `xpc_error`, `xpc_timeout` | Admitted client reports that transport failure; exit 1. xpc_error alone can permit fallback compilation. |
| `xpc_acquisition_failed`, `xpc_submission_refused`, `xpc_protocol_error` | Client reports acquisition failure, reservation refusal or protocol error; exit 1. |
| `runner_client_error` | Another admitted client local-terminal failure; exit 1. |
| `runner_response_unavailable` | Completion has no host result to supply an outcome; exit 1. |
| Other admitted host label | Retain the label and select exit 1; only exact `finished` selects run success. |

`valid` means the applicable controller checks for this projection passed;
`invalid` means they produced a finding. Null means there was no worker
projection to validate. When at least one actor has a worker projection,
actor aggregation is valid when every actor projection is valid or has null
integrity; it becomes invalid when any actor projection is invalid. With no

shared.prose:
An ordinary semantic reply is a reply with no reporting_failure record;
this branch includes both single-worker and actor execution forms.

| Check family | Applicability and checked relationship | Finding scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lifecycle claims | Each worker subprocess: required claims, state/basis references, owned final status, cleanup facts, progress association, slot count/order, action identity, lifecycle copies and supported conflicts. | That worker's projection; ordinary projection or one actor entry. |
| Phase and query evidence | Ordinary semantic reply: phase IDs/order, action partition, collection state, validator ownership and raw-record association, protocol violations, comparison vocabulary and the complete `query_first` chain. | Reply-wide. |
| Policy delivery/read evidence | Ordinary semantic reply with a worker policy-read receipt: bounded counts, host expected-count agreement, length-refusal detail and consistency with later worker observations. | Reply-wide. |
| Native operation observations | Ordinary semantic reply: each fresh-read, fresh-write and exec observation's applicable fields and native relationships. | Reply-wide. |
| Actor association | Ordinary semantic actor reply: actor indexes/IDs, launch/subprocess PID, visits, phase owner, event owner and matching transfer source. | Reply-wide. |
| Actor setup, equipment, application, termination and custody | Ordinary semantic reply: execution-form applicability and the actor record relationships defined by those surfaces. | Reply-wide. |
| Reporting-failure form | A reply carrying reporting_failure: degraded outcome/rc/error, origin/diagnostic/original outcome, removed comparisons and the retention-specific record form. | Reply-wide. |

The reporting-failure branch checks its degradation form while retaining the
assembled records. Worker lifecycle projections still run independently,
with their comparison-limitation requirement waived when the comparison
has been removed by degradation. The retained host records remain
available for inspection at their own observation boundaries.
shared.title: Check families and applicability

while another actor retains a valid clean-exit lifecycle. The controller
then publishes top-level `withheld` and an actor-evidence finding beside
that actor's `clean_exit`. If the admitted host summary is `finished`,
the outer result still reports `ok: true` and exit 0. The three values

`sentinel_deadline`, `done`, `child_reaped`, `wait_error`,
`policy_write_error` or `policy_transfer_deadline`; otherwise null.

finding preserves an already projected ordinary stop reason.

A clean ordinary exit gives null; another ordinary disposition gives

named causes. Actor-form top-level diagnostics begin with null because
causes belong to the actor entries. A reply-wide finding sets this field
to `unknown`.

shared.prose:
Lifecycle claim states are `supported`, `conflicting`, `unresolved` and
`inapplicable`. A supported claim needs an answer and sufficient resolving
basis; unresolved and inapplicable need a reason. A conflicting claim
needs the matching indexed conflict record and native observations.
Another state produces an invalid-claim finding.

Some answers and summaries are open. For example, an unfamiliar
applicability answer or lifecycle summary is retained, while a known
summary is checked against the canonical lifecycle. A supported unfamiliar
final-status answer that passes the other claim checks projects as
`unrecognized`. This differs from an unknown closed claim state, which
withholds the worker projection.
shared.title: Closed claim states and open answers

shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.

shared.prose:
| Operation | Required operands | Producing actor and consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue` | `family`, `target`, `authority`, `token_ref` | Active actor calls native file issuance once with class selected by authority, exact target and flags zero; assigns the declared token resource. |
| `transfer` | `token_ref`, `recipient`, `delivery_ref` | Token-owning actor publishes a host request for one assigned recipient slot; assigns the delivery resource. |
| `consume` | `delivery_ref`, `handle_ref` | Recipient actor calls native consume on its usable delivered token; assigns the handle resource. |
| `release` | `handle_ref` | Consuming actor calls native release for its candidate handle. |

Each other operand must be absent. A required null operand is missing for this grammar; an extraneous null operand is inapplicable.
shared.title: Operation grammar

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
Every controller and compiler-helper envelope carries these string fields
under `build`. They identify the emitting binary's compiled context.
shared.title: Build identification

shared.prose:
The Git HEAD object name observed by the packaged build, or `unknown` when
unavailable. Direct Rust compilation reads `PW_BUILD_COMMIT` with an absent
value falling back to `unknown`. Describe and commit report provenance;
identity admission compares the contract field.
shared.title: Commit

shared.prose:
The public identity embedded in the emitting binary. Receiving boundaries use
the exact value according to their identity-admission rule.
shared.title: Contract

shared.prose:
The descriptive source coordinate compiled into the producer. `build.sh`
uses `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty`, falling back
to `unknown`. Direct Rust compilation reads `PW_BUILD_DESCRIBE` with an absent
value falling back to `unknown`.
shared.title: Describe

shared.prose:
The build-number string. `build.sh` uses nonempty `PW_BUILD_NUMBER` when
supplied, otherwise the Git commit count, falling back to `0`. Direct Rust
compilation reads `PW_BUILD_NUMBER`, falling back to `unknown` when absent.
shared.title: Number

shared.prose:
The packaged build's version string. `build.sh` uses nonempty `PW_VERSION`
when supplied; otherwise it takes the leading three-part version from its
Git describe value, falling back to `0.0.0`. Direct Rust compilation reads
`PW_BUILD_VERSION`, falling back to `unknown` when absent.
shared.title: Version

shared.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
shared.title: Absent field

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
shared.title: Effect

shared.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
shared.title: Null value

shared.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
shared.title: Observation

shared.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
shared.title: Phase

shared.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
shared.title: Prediction

shared.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
shared.title: Request

shared.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
shared.title: Specimen

shared.prose:
Fixed byte length of the CodeDirectory hashes admitted from equipment
inventory and code inspection.
shared.title: CodeDirectory hash byte width

shared.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
shared.title: CodeDirectory hexadecimal width

shared.prose:
Fixed byte length of SHA-256 digests used for the schema fingerprint, worker
identity and signed-file hashes.
shared.title: SHA-256 digest length

shared.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
shared.title: SHA-256 hexadecimal width

shared.prose:
The host's typed reply carries this producer record. Each field comes from the
host's compiled build context.
shared.title: Host producer identification

shared.prose:
The host build's observed Git HEAD object name, or `unknown` when the compiled
context has no such observation. Identity admission uses `contract`; this field
retains the host's provenance.
shared.title: Commit

shared.prose:
The host's public identity, independently compared by a receiver before the
reply's execution records supply interpretations.
shared.title: Contract

shared.prose:
The host build's descriptive Git coordinate, or `unknown` in the ordinary
unbound Swift build context. Packaged context generation supplies the observed
build description.
shared.title: Describe

shared.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.
shared.title: Exact admission identity

shared.prose:
The Rust controller and compiler helper embed a nonempty compile-time
`PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` verbatim. An absent or empty value becomes `unbound`.
Ordinary SwiftPM compilation uses `unbound`; its explicitly selected unit-test
context uses `test:policy-witness`. Rust unit tests likewise use
`test:policy-witness`. A request cannot pass the controller's identity gate
when its expected identity is empty or `unbound`.
shared.title: Direct compilation contexts

shared.prose:
The direct Rust environment path is established by the compile-time constant
and Cargo's environment tracking. The available plain-Cargo integration check
removes `PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` and establishes the unbound case. A direct Cargo
build with an explicitly supplied foreign or release-form identity has not
been exercised in this examination.
shared.title: Direct-build evidence limit

shared.prose:
`release:vX.Y.Z` names the sole annotated release tag at the build checkout's
HEAD. The build derives this form when the checkout is clean, the tag matches
`v<digits>.<digits>.<digits>`, and the selected files' actual bytes and inventory
equal that tag's blobs. More than one qualifying annotated tag on a clean
HEAD refuses identity derivation as ambiguous.

`development:<sha256>` identifies the selected source paths and bytes in
other source trees. Its digest is SHA-256 with the domain prefix
`PolicyWitness public build contract` followed by a NUL byte. For each sorted
repository-relative path, the generator appends the UTF-8 path and file bytes,
each preceded by its unsigned eight-byte big-endian length. A dirty release
checkout receives this development form. A documentation-only edit can change
the form from release to development while leaving the selected-source digest
unchanged.
shared.title: Release and development forms

shared.prose: The controller manages external XPC services through a local registry and launchd. Registry state, on-disk signature observations, live service presence and a completed verification specimen establish different facts. Recovery ownership remains recorded until cleanup observes service and plist absence and publishes that retirement.
shared.title: Managing runners

shared.prose: An empty keys/granted list with an error describes unavailable parsing. Boolean false, strings and integers do not enter granted. Additional members remain opaque.
shared.title: Entitlement observation

shared.title: granted

shared.prose: Sorted names of every key in a parsed entitlement dictionary, regardless of value.

shared.prose: Entitlement plist text returned by codesign, or null when none was emitted or the read was unavailable.

shared.title: Signature observation

shared.title: adhoc

shared.title: cdhash
