shared.prose: TeamIdentifier string read from codesign metadata when available; null when absent.
shared.title: team_id

shared.prose: Recorded success of the owning signature-read/verification path. During validation, host validity also requires recursive bundle verification; each helper requires its own binary verification. Failed metadata reads produce false.
shared.title: valid

shared.prose: Expected IDs are joined only to one accepted record describing the submitted query. Accepted records remain at collection scope when the join cannot select them.
shared.title: Validator query association

shared.prose: Number of accepted records involved: zero for missing_id, one for query_mismatch, the group size for duplicate/unexpected IDs, or total null-ID records for unassociated.
shared.title: count

shared.prose: missing_id, duplicate_id, query_mismatch, unexpected_id or unassociated.
shared.title: kind

shared.prose: runner_host, identifying the component computing the association issue.
shared.title: origin

shared.prose: Expected or unexpected ID concerned by the issue; absent for records whose verdict ID is null.
shared.title: step_id

shared.prose: A step or extension event carries this compact projection of its canonical disposition claims.
shared.title: Per-attempt lifecycle projection

shared.prose: Copy of the owning disposition step's step_boundary_reached claim.
shared.title: boundary

shared.prose: Copy of the owning disposition step's step_result_published claim.
shared.title: result

facts.unknown: The controller retains an unfamiliar summary and checks the independently carried boundary and result claims.

shared.prose: The current producer derives completed, started_without_result, not_reached, unsupported, unresolved or conflicting from the boundary/result claims and attempt support. The controller retains unfamiliar summary strings; it checks the recognized summaries against their corresponding claims.
shared.title: summary

shared.prose: A supported claim names its answer and observation references. An unresolved or inapplicable claim names its reason; a conflicting claim points to its issue.
shared.title: Lifecycle claim

shared.prose: Question-specific supported answer, such as signal, exit_code, reached, published or an observed host stop reason.
shared.title: answer

shared.prose: Observation references supporting the answer or explaining uncertainty: raw run fields, progress, worker_failure, plan, slot and attempt_support in their question's scope.
shared.title: basis

shared.prose: Zero-based pointer to the matching conflict in disposition.issues.
shared.title: issue

shared.prose: Reason the question is unresolved or inapplicable, preserving missing, unusable, nonterminal and unsupported evidence distinctions.
shared.title: reason

shared.prose: supported, unresolved, conflicting or inapplicable, determining which accompanying fields carry the claim.
shared.title: state

shared.prose: Answer payload: an exit code, signal or item index as an integer, or the observed termination-request object.
shared.title: value

shared.prose: The integer alternative carries a signal, exit code or index according to the question. The request alternative carries the complete host termination request.
shared.title: Lifecycle answer value

shared.prose: The host retains the first fault and its exact received byte context. Earlier accepted verdicts remain available.
shared.title: Rejected validator frame

shared.prose: Zero-based offset of the rejected frame's first byte in received stdout.
shared.title: byte_offset

shared.prose: Base64 encoding of the retained received-byte prefix. Decoding yields those exact bytes.
shared.title: context_b64

shared.prose: True when frame_bytes exceeds retained_bytes.
shared.title: context_truncated

shared.prose: Length of that frame in bytes, excluding its LF separator.
shared.title: frame_bytes

shared.prose: Receiver category utf8, json or structure for the first rejected frame.
shared.title: kind

shared.prose: Human-readable reason the frame failed structural admission.
shared.title: message

shared.prose: runner_host, identifying the rejecting receiver.
shared.title: origin

shared.prose: Number of prefix bytes retained, capped at 256.
shared.title: retained_bytes

shared.prose: The host exposes text only after acquiring a complete or truncated publication with a bounded length and terminating NUL.
shared.title: Worker diagnostic

shared.prose: Retained diagnostic-byte length excluding its terminating NUL, at most <!-- span limits.worker_diagnostic.value_unit -->4,095 bytes<!-- /span --> when validation permits text extraction.
shared.title: length

facts.unknown: The numeric value remains in the report. Known-branch assessments require their own recognized code and publication conditions.

shared.prose: Raw diagnostic publication word: 0 absent, 1 complete, 2 truncated, 3 incomplete; other values remain numeric.
shared.title: state

shared.prose: Host interpretation: absent, incomplete, unknown, complete, truncated or invalid. Invalid identifies an eligible publication whose length or terminator failed validation.
shared.title: status

shared.prose: Diagnostic bytes decoded as UTF-8 with replacement for invalid sequences. The <!-- span limits.worker_diagnostic.value_unit -->4,095 bytes<!-- /span --> bound applies before replacement decoding. The diagnostic status carries whether the worker truncated its buffer.
shared.title: text

shared.prose: The host resolves this account once from the worker's acquired output and submitted plan. Run questions and per-step questions keep their individual support and conflicts.
shared.title: Canonical worker disposition

shared.prose: Conflicting observations referenced by conflicting claims; indices are zero-based within this array.
shared.title: issues

shared.prose: Fixed set of run-level lifecycle claims.
shared.title: questions

context.where: final worker output and plan join

facts.free.condition: Resolve each question from the owning worker's acquired output, unique slot identities and submitted plan. A not_reached or unpublished conclusion requires terminal collection where specified below.
facts.free.effect: Publish the canonical account once and copy its boundary/result claims into per-attempt lifecycle projections. Retain conflicts as issues rather than selecting one conflicting observation.
facts.where: final worker output and plan join

shared.prose:
An exit code or signal is supported after a successful reap. Both representations
produce a D1 conflict. A completed supported slot establishes publication and
can establish entry. Recognized progress at or after an attempt's entry also
establishes entry. A final earlier progress position establishes `not_reached`
only after confirmed reaping and with an incomplete slot; beside a completed
slot it produces D5. Returned-or-later terminal progress beside an incomplete
supported slot produces D5 for result publication. Live collection leaves
missing results unresolved. An unsupported attempt has inapplicable result
publication and an `unsupported` lifecycle summary.
shared.title: Resolving lifecycle claims

shared.prose: Plan-ordered lifecycle claims for each requested step, joined only to uniquely identified worker slots.
shared.title: steps

shared.prose: A completed worker exec slot separates collection, cleanup requests and the owned leader reap. Collection facts are frozen before termination requests.
shared.title: Spawned-command observation

shared.prose: Requests to terminate the spawned process group and any leader fallback.
shared.title: cleanup

shared.prose: Leader-exit and pipe observations up to the collection stop.
shared.title: collection

shared.prose: Final bounded wait account for the owned leader after collection and cleanup.
shared.title: reap

shared.prose: Cleanup requests follow the frozen collection observation and preserve their native returns.
shared.title: Exec cleanup

shared.prose: SIGKILL request to negative leader PID for the owned process group, when cleanup is requested.
shared.title: group_request

shared.prose: SIGKILL request to the positive leader PID after a failed group request with errno other than ESRCH.
shared.title: leader_fallback

shared.prose: not_requested after leader_exit_and_eof; ownership_unconfirmed when waitid failed; requested when an eligible process-group cleanup was attempted.
shared.title: state

shared.prose: The collector can observe leader exit and pipe EOF independently; descendants may keep a stream open after the leader exits.
shared.title: Exec collection

shared.prose: Local numeric clock-fault observation when collection stopped for failed/backward time.
shared.title: clock_fault

shared.prose: child or plan when the selected collection deadline expires; absent on other stop branches. The child allowance and remaining per-worker active-plan allowance are defined by the exec operation.
shared.title: deadline_kind

shared.prose: Whether waitid observed the owned leader's exit during collection.
shared.title: leader_exit_observed

shared.prose: Native poll failure which stopped stream observation; recovered EINTR is excluded.
shared.title: poll_errno

shared.prose: EOF or native read/poll failure retained for stderr.
shared.title: stderr

shared.prose: EOF or native read/poll failure retained for stdout.
shared.title: stdout

shared.prose: leader_exit_and_eof, deadline, observation_error or clock_fault, recording the branch that stopped collection.
shared.title: stop_reason

shared.prose: Native waitid failure which stopped leader observation; recovered EINTR is excluded.
shared.title: waitid_errno

shared.prose: Final wait facts concern the spawned leader owned by the worker. After collection ends, the production reap allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_reap_grace.value_unit -->1,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> of continuous time. Earlier ownership or group-request failures retain their branch priority; a recorded request and an observed reap remain separate.
shared.title: Exec leader reap

shared.prose: Local numeric clock fault encountered by the reap wait, when observed.
shared.title: clock_fault

shared.prose: Last native waitpid result, with status only when the owned leader PID returned.
shared.title: last_wait

shared.prose: reaped, wait_error, ownership_unconfirmed, group_request_failed, clock_fault or deadline; branch priority preserves earlier ownership/group-request failures.
shared.title: stop_reason

shared.prose: This is the worker's native kill call for a spawned command, scoped to the target named here.
shared.title: Exec signal request

shared.prose: Positive native errno captured for rc -1; absent after success.
shared.title: errno

shared.prose: Native kill return, zero or -1.
shared.title: rc

shared.prose: Signal passed to kill; the exec cleanup path uses SIGKILL.
shared.title: signal

shared.prose: Negative leader PID for a process-group request, or positive leader PID for the fallback request.
shared.title: target

shared.prose: A stream carries EOF or a terminal read/poll observation from collection.
shared.title: Exec stream observation

shared.prose: Whether the worker read EOF on this stream before collection stopped.
shared.title: eof

shared.prose: Terminal error/invalid descriptor poll bits retained when they ended observation; ordinary readable/EOF handling uses its own read observation.
shared.title: poll_revents

shared.prose: Terminal read errno, excluding recovered EINTR and EAGAIN.
shared.title: read_errno

shared.prose: Pending, failed and reaped waits retain their different native return values.
shared.title: Exec leader wait result

shared.prose: Positive captured errno for rc -1, including EINTR; absent otherwise.
shared.title: errno

shared.prose: Native waitpid return: zero pending, -1 failure, or owned leader PID when reaped.
shared.title: rc

shared.prose: Raw terminal wait status present exactly when rc is the owned leader PID, agreeing with the attempt's leader exit/signal fields.
shared.title: status

shared.prose: The worker publishes the operation's native observation and a PW failure classification. Numeric codes retain unfamiliar values.
shared.title: Terminal worker failure

facts.unknown: The numeric value remains in the report. Known-branch assessments require their own recognized code and publication conditions.

shared.prose: PW failure classification within that operation.
shared.title: code

facts.unknown: The numeric value remains in the report. Known-branch assessments require their own recognized code and publication conditions.

shared.prose: Additional operation-specific numeric classification retained alongside the primary failure code.
shared.title: detail

shared.prose: Native errno when the publication marks it present.
shared.title: errno

shared.prose:
The host binds each validator collection to its phase and retains accepted records through later I/O, association or cleanup failure.

For N submitted queries, the collector assigns a record allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_records_per_query.value -->2<!-- /span --> and a stdout retention allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_reply_bytes_per_query.value_unit -->16,384 bytes<!-- /span -->. The allowances are sized before writing the query batch. On byte overflow the host counts all bytes received, keeps the bounded prefix through its last complete LF frame, closes collection and reports byte_limit. Decoding retains complete accepted records before the first refused frame or record-count excess.
shared.title: Validator subprocess

facts.free.condition: Join each expected ID to exactly one accepted record whose supplied query metadata agrees; allow/deny additionally require the complete submitted query identity.
facts.free.effect: Exclude ambiguous, missing or mismatched records from the per-step join, retain every accepted record in the collection and publish association_issues.

shared.prose:
Duplicate IDs leave every record of that group at collection scope. Null IDs
remain unassociated. Diagnostic outcomes may omit query metadata; any supplied
metadata must agree. A decoding fault retains the accepted prefix and the
rejected frame's bounded byte context. Transport or later cleanup failure
preserves the already accepted observations.

Files named by imports can change between these independent reads. A literal inventory describes the producer's walk; the worker compiled-profile receipt has its own observation boundary.

Whether to align that behavior, and how to dispose of that diagnostic in the worker branch, remains unresolved.

shared.prose:
A source may combine a parameter with a literal suffix:

```scheme
(version 1)
(deny default)
(allow file-read* (literal (string-append (param "ROOT") "/hosts")))
```

`"params":{"ROOT":"/etc"}` supplies the value used by this expression. An unused `OPTIONAL` parameter and a referenced but missing `ROOT` exercise different compiler paths. Inspect the native compile record for the latter's outcome.
shared.title: Parameter expressions

facts.free.effect: Sort parameter keys, transport their complete strings, create native parameters only for a nonempty map, and pass each key and value through sandbox_set_param before compiling the selected source. Report setup or compile failure at the observed native stage.

shared.prose: A supplied parameter is data for the SBPL compiler. The compiler decides how source expressions use it. Source text, selected parameter values and imported file bytes are distinct inputs.
shared.title: Prepare native compiler input

shared.prose: Optional string-to-string compiler parameter map. Omission, null and an empty map produce no native parameter setup. Supplied names remain open data. At most <!-- span limits.policy_parameters.value_unit -->1,024 items<!-- /span --> fit each policy, with keys bounded by <!-- span limits.parameter_key.value_unit -->127 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and values by <!-- span limits.parameter_value.value_unit -->383 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->; native strings must be NUL-free.
shared.title: params

shared.prose: Required string when applying a policy. An empty string reaches native compilation. The final source after augmentation fits <!-- span limits.policy_source.value_unit -->262,143 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span -->, and embedded NUL is refused before child launch.
shared.title: sbpl_source

facts.free.effect: After application or an actor's unapplied declaration, acquire stdout/stderr pipes and spawn actions for this released attempt, release them on setup failure and at completion, and report the failing setup call when spawning was prevented. Spawn with target as argv[0], an empty environment, /dev/null stdin, captured stdout/stderr, close-on-exec descriptor policy and a new process group.

shared.prose: A successful spawn supplies a child PID even if the child later exits nonzero. The child collection, termination request and owned reap remain separate observations. The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.

shared.prose: The worker operation implementations and exec setup branches were read. shared.prose:
The worker runs the selected operation after policy application in an apply worker, or after the unapplied actor's setup:

| Kind / action | Native operation and operation-specific consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `file / open_read` | `open(O_RDONLY)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte read and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; read and close results are discarded. |
| `file / open_write` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_TRUNC)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte `x` write and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; write and close results are discarded. |
| `file / create` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CREAT, 0600)` then close. Creation mode is subject to umask. An existing file is opened without truncation or exclusive creation. |
| `file / read_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_RDONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)`, `fstat`, one read bounded by <!-- span limits.fresh_read_bytes.value_unit -->64 bytes<!-- /span -->, then close. Record each boundary and read bytes; aggregate failure selects stat, read or close failure after a successful open. |
| `file / write_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)` of an existing target, opened `fstat`, `ftruncate(0)`, truncated `fstat`, one-byte `x` write after successful truncation, written `fstat`, then close. Preserve the first failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / create_fresh` | `lstat` before a fresh exclusive `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC \| O_CREAT \| O_EXCL, 0600)`, opened `fstat`, one-byte `x` write, written `fstat`, then close. Pre-open `lstat` is an independent observation. Preserve the first operation failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / unlink` | `unlink(target)` and its return/errno. |
| `file / access` | `access(target, R_OK)` and its return/errno. This is an access-check observation. |
| `mach / lookup` | Obtain the task bootstrap port and call `bootstrap_look_up` for the supplied name; release the returned service port on success. |
| `sysctl / read` | One `sysctlbyname` call with a <!-- span limits.sysctl_read_bytes.value_unit -->4,096 bytes<!-- /span --> buffer acquired after application. Report the call's result and errno; discard value bytes and the returned length. |
| `exec / spawn` | Prepare per-attempt child resources, call `posix_spawn` for the absolute target with the requested argv, then collect child and cleanup observations. |

A short fresh write records its native count and fails the aggregate while retaining zero native errno when the write returned a short nonnegative count. A fresh file descriptor belongs to that attempt and is closed before its result is published.
shared.title: Native operations

Present for `execution_form: "actors"`, in the host's actor order. Each
entry is derived from that actor's subprocess and its actions selected
through the phase plan. A reply-wide finding preserves these already
computed actor entries.
nodes.title: actors

context.where: client delivery, public reply identity and bounded response context

facts.free.effect: Check request-delivery failure and client capture status, then exact reply identity, response geometry and compiled-profile context before execution diagnostics. A failed response-context check reports malformed_runner_response and exit 1 with the decoded host reply retained and execution diagnostics omitted.
facts.where: client delivery, public reply identity and bounded response context

nodes.prose:
A missing or foreign producer identity follows its own transport/identity
refusal. The geometry guard bounds collections before semantic joins.
The compiled-profile guard checks its status and producer/stage context,
including actor captures and reporting-failure replies. These are
preconditions for the execution-assessment path described here.
nodes.title: Admit the response before assessment

nodes.prose:
`valid` means the applicable controller checks for this projection passed;
`invalid` means they produced a finding. Null means there was no worker
projection to validate. When at least one actor has a worker projection,
actor aggregation is valid when every actor projection is valid or has null
integrity; it becomes invalid when any actor projection is invalid. With no
worker projections, aggregate integrity remains null. A reply-wide finding
also sets invalid.
A host's supported conflict can accompany valid integrity: the controller
has checked the conflict's own evidence.
nodes.title: disposition_integrity

nodes.prose:
Controller findings at this scope, followed or preceded according to the
producing check order by copied host conflict records where applicable.
Copied host conflicts preserve rule, question, step index and observations.
A nonempty list can accompany valid integrity when its records are
validated host conflicts. Actor-local findings remain in the actor entry.
nodes.title: disposition_issues

nodes.prose:
An ordinary semantic reply is a reply with no reporting_failure record;
this branch includes both single-worker and actor execution forms.

| Check family | Applicability and checked relationship | Finding scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lifecycle claims | Each worker subprocess: required claims, state/basis references, owned final status, cleanup facts, progress association, slot count/order, action identity, lifecycle copies and supported conflicts. | That worker's projection; ordinary projection or one actor entry. |
| Phase and query evidence | Ordinary semantic reply: phase IDs/order, action partition, collection state, validator ownership and raw-record association, protocol violations, comparison vocabulary and the complete `query_first` chain. | Reply-wide. |
| Policy delivery/read evidence | Ordinary semantic reply with a worker policy-read receipt: bounded counts, host expected-count agreement, length-refusal detail and consistency with later worker observations. | Reply-wide. |
| Native operation observations | Ordinary semantic reply: each fresh-read, fresh-write and exec observation's applicable fields and native relationships. | Reply-wide. |
| Actor association | Ordinary semantic actor reply: actor indexes/IDs, launch/subprocess PID, visits, phase owner, event owner and matching transfer source. | Reply-wide. |
| Actor setup, equipment, application, termination and custody | Ordinary semantic reply: execution-form applicability and the actor record relationships defined by those surfaces. | Reply-wide. |
| Reporting-failure form | A reply carrying reporting_failure: degraded outcome/rc/error, origin/diagnostic/original outcome, removed comparisons and the retention-specific record form. | Reply-wide. |

The reporting-failure branch checks its degradation form while retaining the
assembled records. Worker lifecycle projections still run independently,
with their comparison-limitation requirement waived when the comparison
has been removed by degradation. The retained host records remain
available for inspection at their own observation boundaries.
nodes.title: Check families and applicability

nodes.prose:
The envelope's result-selection rule governs completion. Individual failed
attempts and controller integrity findings remain visible beside that result.
A reply-wide withheld disposition can therefore accompany an outer successful
result.
nodes.title: Findings beside the completion result

nodes.prose:
The controller's disposition projection. An ordinary worker supplies its
validated lifecycle result. Actor execution uses `per_actor` when at least
one actor has a worker projection; each actor's entry supplies that ending.
A reply-wide finding sets this field to `withheld`. `no_worker` means this
projection had no worker subprocess record to assess.
nodes.title: process_disposition

context.where: typed worker lifecycle interpretation after response admission

facts.free.effect: Validate each worker's lifecycle against its native records and assigned actions. If that worker's validation produces any finding, set its process_disposition to withheld, termination_cause to unknown and disposition_integrity to invalid, with stop_reason null. Otherwise derive the ending from final_status and preserve validated host conflicts.
facts.where: typed worker lifecycle interpretation after response admission

nodes.prose:
For the actor form, the controller computes each worker's projection
separately. It then sets the top-level disposition to `per_actor` when any
entry differs from `no_worker`, and aggregates the actor integrity values.
This calculation occurs before the reply-wide checks below.
nodes.title: Project one worker or aggregate actors

nodes.prose:
The host self-check, controller reader and harness reader are separate
implementations of the public relationships. The prior constructed
comparison found divergent judgments. Shared acceptance and refusal
controls still need to be reconciled around each rule's applicability,
including preparation failures and reporting failures. This draft credits
the controller branches and inspected controls above; integrated release
execution remains to be attached.
nodes.title: Shared reader evidence

context.where: typed reply relationship checks after worker projections

facts.free.condition: One or more applicable reply-wide checks finds an invalid relationship.
facts.where: typed reply relationship checks after worker projections

nodes.prose:
The controller appends these findings to top-level `disposition_issues`.
It preserves the actor entries, an ordinary stop reason already derived,
and all host fields including step comparisons and claimed gate outcomes.
Those retained assertions can therefore appear beside the controller's
finding about them. The finding's level determines which controller
projection changes.
nodes.title: Apply reply-wide findings

nodes.prose:
A typed actor reply can carry a transfer naming an invalid source actor,
while another actor retains a valid clean-exit lifecycle. The controller
then publishes top-level `withheld` and an actor-evidence finding beside
that actor's `clean_exit`. If the admitted host summary is `finished`,
the outer result still reports `ok: true` and exit 0. The three values
answer the reply relationship, individual ending and host completion
questions respectively.
nodes.title: Scope example

nodes.prose:
Supported ordinary-worker stop observation when its answer is one of
`sentinel_deadline`, `done`, `child_reaped`, `wait_error`,
`policy_write_error` or `policy_transfer_deadline`; otherwise null.
Actor stop reasons belong to their actor entries. A later reply-wide
finding preserves an already projected ordinary stop reason.
nodes.title: stop_reason

nodes.prose:
A controller attribution selected from the validated lifecycle chain.
A clean ordinary exit gives null; another ordinary disposition gives
`unknown` until the host-cleanup conditions below establish one of the
named causes. Actor-form top-level diagnostics begin with null because
causes belong to the actor entries. A reply-wide finding sets this field
to `unknown`.
nodes.title: termination_cause

nodes.prose:
Lifecycle claim states are `supported`, `conflicting`, `unresolved` and
`inapplicable`. A supported claim needs an answer and sufficient resolving
basis; unresolved and inapplicable need a reason. A conflicting claim
needs the matching indexed conflict record and native observations.
Another state produces an invalid-claim finding.

Some answers and summaries are open. For example, an unfamiliar
applicability answer or lifecycle summary is retained, while a known
summary is checked against the canonical lifecycle. A supported unfamiliar
final-status answer that passes the other claim checks projects as
`unrecognized`. This differs from an unknown closed claim state, which
withholds the worker projection.
nodes.title: Closed claim states and open answers

nodes.prose:
Human-readable explanation of the failed relationship or copied host
conflict. Some controller details embed a step label or position; other
actor and gate findings carry a general explanation.
nodes.title: detail

facts.unknown: An unfamiliar category remains a finding with its carried detail and scope; interpreting its specific condition requires that producer's definition.

nodes.prose:
Category supplied by the controller check or copied from a host conflict.
A finding's origin and effect follow the producing scope and the remaining
fields, rather than an exhaustive match over this list.

Host observation-reference list copied from a validated conflict.
Controller-created findings currently omit this field.
nodes.title: observations

Host question associated with a copied conflict. Controller-created
findings currently omit this field even when a detail names the question.
nodes.title: question

facts.free.effect: Publish controller findings as kind and detail. Copy validated host conflicts with their rule, question, step index and observation references. Preserve the host reply independently of both forms.

nodes.prose:
Host conflict rule copied from the retained disposition issue, such as
D1 for a final-status conflict or D5 for the supported step conflicts.
Controller-created findings currently omit this field.
nodes.title: rule

nodes.prose:
Worker-local step index copied from a host conflict when it has step
scope. A copied run-level conflict and controller-created findings omit it.
nodes.title: step_index

nodes.prose:
Controller-generated findings currently identify their affected phase or
actor through surrounding scope and, where supplied, human detail.
A structured reference to the specific phase, actor or assertion remains
unimplemented. Adding that reference must preserve the existing distinction
between worker-local projection findings and reply-wide findings.

context.where: selected runner/helper paths and embedded evidence manifest

facts.free.condition: Runner selection supplies paths and the app evidence manifest supplies role baselines where available.

For another selected file, attempt its hash and compare it with the role baseline; retain independent availability and error facts. After a dossier-only collection failure or hash mismatch, continue preparation and invocation subject to the separate selection and admission results.
facts.where: selected runner/helper paths and embedded evidence manifest

nodes.prose: A role baseline must be the unique entry at the expected path and kind with a 64-digit hexadecimal SHA-256. `match` means selected on-disk bytes matched that baseline at this read. A null role record refers to the shipped manifest description; ordinary collection does not rehash that shipped file. Worker/validator override strings must be absolute to be read; NUL-containing or over-<!-- span limits.test_override_path.value -->1,023<!-- /span -->-byte overrides are neither echoed nor opened. Optional `PW_VERIFY_EVIDENCE=1` separately hashes the manifest entries carrying declared hashes.
nodes.title: Compare selected files

context.where: request preparation before runner-client invocation and fallback compile

facts.free.condition: A request has been parsed and controller policy changes have been resolved in memory.
facts.free.effect: Serialize the held selected request once and use those bytes for client delivery and whole-request fallback compilation. Derive source hashes from its decoded UTF-8 sbpl_source string and retain the dossier even when later preparation or invocation fails.
facts.where: request preparation before runner-client invocation and fallback compile

nodes.prose: The original path is a locator. JSON whitespace, escape spelling and subsequent edits to that file have no role in the held source hash. Actor fallback checks serialize the held resolved policy objects separately in request order. A later helper import scan can observe different import-file bytes because those files are independently opened. Actor-form dossiers retain request order; malformed identity/mode fields become null and policy availability remains distinct from admission.
nodes.title: Hold the selected request

nodes.prose: If a caller changes the input JSON after the controller has parsed it, the client and fallback compiler still receive the controller’s held serialization. An import file changed between dossier collection and fallback compilation may produce different import observations. Compare the source hash and the separately reported closures at their named boundaries.
nodes.title: Held-file example

nodes.prose: The scanner’s `complete` status exhausts its literal import search. Its search order follows the recorded platform convention; collision precedence and parity with native compilation remain unverified. A signed held-request change experiment and independent observations tying selected-file hashes to executing images remain open.
nodes.title: Import and execution evidence

context.where: selected policy source and local import files before invocation

facts.free.condition: The selected policy has string source within the <!-- span limits.helper_source.binary -->4 MiB<!-- /span --> source bound.
facts.free.effect: Scan literal import forms, resolve absolute names as given and relative names under /System/Library/Sandbox/Profiles then /usr/share/sandbox, and record observed reads within depth 8 and count 64. Mark unresolved names, nonliteral forms, cycles, decoding failures and bound hits as incomplete.
facts.where: selected policy source and local import files before invocation

nodes.prose: Names retain their spelling, including a `.sb` suffix when supplied. Resolution deduplicates canonical paths and unresolved names. A file is opened once with nonblocking open, checked as regular through that descriptor, and read for both hashing and recursive scanning. Records sort by resolved path, then unresolved name. The closure hash is SHA-256 of selected source UTF-8 bytes, byte `0x1f`, then sorted `resolved_path + " " + sha256` lines joined with LF for records having both values. This identifies the scanned material even when the scan is incomplete.

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
A byte field identifies its byte source, encoding, total/retained length and
bound where applicable. Hexadecimal and base64 are representations of bytes;
decoded diagnostic text is a separate projection. UTF-8 byte counts and
character counts use the units named by each capacity.
shared.title: Byte observation

shared.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
shared.title: Request

shared.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
shared.title: Specimen

context.where: external bundle validation, signing, registry and launchd

facts.free.condition: The caller supplies an existing bundle directory; the kind defaults to byoxpc, and an explicit kind must be byoxpc. Scope defaults to user or may be explicitly system.
facts.free.effect: Resolve the canonical bundle, require CFBundlePackageType XPC!, exact current PWContract, CFBundleIdentifier service identity and an existing Contents/MacOS/CFBundleExecutable. Reject conflicting active/recovery service, bundle or executable identities; verify the source seal and equipment inventory before optional signing.
facts.where: external bundle validation, signing, registry and launchd

nodes.prose: An explicit service name must equal the bundle identifier. `--bundle-id` and `--executable` are refused; those identities come from the bundle. The installer refuses an existing target plist. With `--identity`, it signs the selected worker and host with the supplied entitlements, and the validator/unentitled worker without them, refreshing the sealed equipment inventory before sealing the host. Entitlements with `--allow-adhoc` can select ad-hoc signing; an ad-hoc result requires that flag. Required helpers must exist. Absent resources are classified ambiguous for ownership and retain their independently observed absent presence. Unknown presence produces unknown ownership. Recorded cleanup paths must be absolute, have no parent traversal, end in the expected service plist, and have an immediate parent named LaunchAgents for user scope or LaunchDaemons for system scope. The location check also requires the executable parent to equal the recorded bundle’s Contents/MacOS and refuses symlinked plist ancestors. The recorded ownership supplies the full parent path. Legacy records without ownership derive the conventional plist path and use the content checks.

nodes.prose: User scope writes HOME/Library/LaunchAgents and targets gui/<uid>, requiring access to that logged-in GUI domain. The plist invokes the recorded executable with `--mach-service` and the service name, advertises that Mach service, sets RunAtLoad and a <!-- span limits.byoxpc_throttle_interval.value_unit -->1 second<!-- /span --> throttle, and defaults XPC_SERVICE_PATH to the bundle. `--env KEY=VALUE` requires a nonempty key; later occurrences replace earlier values. With `--skip-bootstrap`, successful plist creation completes installation; `loaded` remains a separate observation. Signing changes can precede the pending save.

A changed/unreadable/unowned object, failed action or failed retirement publication retains recovery and warnings. A repeated remove continues the retained record, including after the plist has disappeared. `--skip-bootout` can remove an owned plist; retirement still requires observed service absence. The dependency wait observes the owned source child without requesting its
departure. Its budget is the lesser of <!-- span limits.actor_termination_wait.value_unit -->5,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> and the remaining
execution allowance in whole milliseconds. Deadline samples and final elapsed
accounting govern satisfaction. These are charged-wait conditions; operating
system scheduling determines when the host next runs.

`termination_dependency:<outcome>`. Later phases retain their declarations

shared.prose:
The scheduler includes inspection in its shared <!-- span limits.actor_setup_allowance.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> monotonic setup allowance. It requires valid clock samples before and after each inspection and records inspection_deadline, cancelling scheduling, when an otherwise successful inspection reaches or exceeds that setup deadline. Before the scheduler runs, orchestration also attempts to establish an additional monotonic deadline <!-- span limits.actor_lifetime_cutoff.value_unit -->180,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> from that initial clock sample, reusing the configured actor-lifetime duration. This additional deadline has its own clock and origin, separate from the workers' shared continuous-clock cutoff. When its initial sample is unavailable, the additional deadline comparison is absent; the scheduler's setup guard and the inspection's valid start/final clock samples still apply. When present, the additional deadline requires both inspection samples strictly before it.

Inspection retains each attempted native call and stops at its first failed
boundary. A later inspection failure preserves an earlier cancellation reason
already selected by the scheduler. Static `bound` and live `matched` express
their respective observations; the signature entitlement dictionary supplies
the values assessed at each boundary.

shared.prose:
| Operation | Required operands | Producing actor and consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issue` | `family`, `target`, `authority`, `token_ref` | Active actor calls native file issuance once with class selected by authority, exact target and flags zero; assigns the declared token resource. |
| `transfer` | `token_ref`, `recipient`, `delivery_ref` | Token-owning actor publishes a host request for one assigned recipient slot; assigns the delivery resource. |
| `consume` | `delivery_ref`, `handle_ref` | Recipient actor calls native consume on its usable delivered token; assigns the handle resource. |
| `release` | `handle_ref` | Consuming actor calls native release for its candidate handle. |

Each other operand must be absent. A required null operand is missing for this grammar; an extraneous null operand is inapplicable.

shared.prose:
PolicyWitness accepts a specimen, runs its declared sandbox experiment and
reports the observations and assessments obtained at each boundary. The
contract identifies the component responsible for each action, the conditions
under which it acts, and the meaning of the resulting records.
shared.title: The contract identity

shared.prose:
Every controller and compiler-helper envelope carries these string fields
under `build`. They identify the emitting binary's compiled context.
shared.title: Build identification

shared.prose:
The Git HEAD object name observed by the packaged build, or `unknown` when
unavailable. Direct Rust compilation reads `PW_BUILD_COMMIT` with an absent
value falling back to `unknown`. Describe and commit report provenance;
identity admission compares the contract field.
shared.title: Commit

shared.prose:
The descriptive source coordinate compiled into the producer. `build.sh`
uses `git describe --tags --match 'v[0-9]*' --always --dirty`, falling back
to `unknown`. Direct Rust compilation reads `PW_BUILD_DESCRIBE` with an absent
value falling back to `unknown`.
shared.title: Describe

shared.prose:
A field is absent when its key is omitted from the JSON object. The field's
definition determines whether omission selects a default, means unavailable
information, makes the object inapplicable or refuses the input.
shared.title: Absent field

shared.prose:
The runner client acquires a reservation, submits the held request over XPC
and returns a typed capture of its transport observations and received host
bytes. The controller invokes it once for a run.
shared.title: Runner client

shared.prose:
`policy-witness` reads and prepares the request, selects equipment, invokes the
runner client, admits its records and emits the outer JSON envelope. Its
dossier and assessments are controller observations and interpretations.
shared.title: Controller

shared.prose:
An effect is an observable consequence of an operation, such as creation of a
file, truncation, bytes read or written, or spawning a child. Each effect claim
is bounded by its concrete observation: descriptor metadata, content/transfer
result, child PID or independent state observation. An `open_write` success
reports its truncating open; the worker discards the following write's return.
The meaning of a successful status is specific to that operation.
shared.title: Effect

shared.prose:
`null` is an explicitly carried JSON value. Its equivalence to omission is a
field-specific rule. In output, a null observation leaves the represented
fact unavailable unless that field defines a more specific meaning.
shared.title: Null value

shared.prose:
An observation records what a named component read, returned, published or
reaped at a particular boundary. Its result, origin, subject and available
timing determine its evidentiary scope. A missing publication leaves the
operation's result unresolved even when progress indicates that it began.
shared.title: Observation

shared.prose:
A phase groups an ordered batch of actions under one worker or actor visit.
The host's query collection precedes release of the phase's action batch
under the ordering rules. Phase completion and individual action completion
are separate observations.
shared.title: Phase

shared.prose:
A prediction is the usable result of a native sandbox query for the reported
worker, operation and filter at collection time. Excluded queries, diagnostics
and missing validator results carry their own unavailable/error observations.
`query_first` establishes a supported ordering interval before an action
batch; changes of state inside that interval remain possible.
shared.title: Prediction

shared.prose:
A request is the value presented at an entry boundary. The controller holds
the parsed request, resolves controller-owned options and sends a serialization
of the resulting value. Submitted bytes and original file bytes are distinct
artifacts; each byte observation names the artifact it covers.
shared.title: Request

shared.prose:
A specimen is the declared experiment: its identifier, asserted contract,
policy or actor policies, ordered phases/actions, and accepted execution
options. A saved specimen is its JSON representation in a request file.
shared.title: Specimen

shared.prose:
Fixed byte length of the CodeDirectory hashes admitted from equipment
inventory and code inspection.
shared.title: CodeDirectory hash byte width

shared.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
shared.title: CodeDirectory hexadecimal width

shared.prose:
Fixed byte length of SHA-256 digests used for the schema fingerprint, worker
identity and signed-file hashes.
shared.title: SHA-256 digest length

shared.prose: Character length of their lowercase hexadecimal representation.
shared.title: SHA-256 hexadecimal width

shared.prose:
The host's typed reply carries this producer record. Each field comes from the
host's compiled build context.
shared.title: Host producer identification

shared.prose:
The host build's observed Git HEAD object name, or `unknown` when the compiled
context has no such observation. Identity admission uses `contract`; this field
retains the host's provenance.
shared.title: Commit

shared.prose:
The host's public identity, independently compared by a receiver before the
reply's execution records supply interpretations.
shared.title: Contract

shared.prose:
The host build's descriptive Git coordinate, or `unknown` in the ordinary
unbound Swift build context. Packaged context generation supplies the observed
build description.
shared.title: Describe

shared.prose:
A public contract identity is the string a build embeds for exact admission.
A specimen carries it in `contract`; controller and compiler-helper envelopes
carry it in `build.contract`; a host reply carries it in `producer.contract`;
a client capture carries its own producer identity. The app and service
property lists carry the build's value as `PWContract`. At an identity-admission
boundary, the receiver compares the arriving identity with its expected identity.
Equality supplies that boundary's identity match. Request validity, wire
structure, equipment association and supported observations have their own
conditions.
shared.title: Exact admission identity

shared.prose:
The Rust controller and compiler helper embed a nonempty compile-time
`PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` verbatim. An absent or empty value becomes `unbound`.
Ordinary SwiftPM compilation uses `unbound`; its explicitly selected unit-test
context uses `test:policy-witness`. Rust unit tests likewise use
`test:policy-witness`. A request cannot pass the controller's identity gate
when its expected identity is empty or `unbound`.
shared.title: Direct compilation contexts

shared.prose:
The direct Rust environment path is established by the compile-time constant
and Cargo's environment tracking. The available plain-Cargo integration check
removes `PW_BUILD_CONTRACT` and establishes the unbound case. A direct Cargo
build with an explicitly supplied foreign or release-form identity has not
been exercised in this examination.
shared.title: Direct-build evidence limit

shared.prose:
`release:vX.Y.Z` names the sole annotated release tag at the build checkout's
HEAD. The build derives this form when the checkout is clean, the tag matches
`v<digits>.<digits>.<digits>`, and the selected files' actual bytes and inventory
equal that tag's blobs. More than one qualifying annotated tag on a clean
HEAD refuses identity derivation as ambiguous.

`development:<sha256>` identifies the selected source paths and bytes in
other source trees. Its digest is SHA-256 with the domain prefix
`PolicyWitness public build contract` followed by a NUL byte. For each sorted
repository-relative path, the generator appends the UTF-8 path and file bytes,
each preceded by its unsigned eight-byte big-endian length. A dirty release
checkout receives this development form. A documentation-only edit can change
the form from release to development while leaving the selected-source digest
unchanged.
shared.title: Release and development forms

shared.prose: Expected IDs are joined only to one accepted record describing the submitted query. Accepted records remain at collection scope when the join cannot select them.

The controller retains unfamiliar summary strings; it checks the recognized summaries against their corresponding claims.

shared.title: Lifecycle claim

shared.title: reason

shared.prose: supported, unresolved, conflicting or inapplicable, determining which accompanying fields carry the claim.
shared.title: state

shared.prose: Answer payload: an exit code, signal or item index as an integer, or the observed termination-request object.
shared.title: value

shared.prose: The integer alternative carries a signal, exit code or index according to the question. The request alternative carries the complete host termination request.
shared.title: Lifecycle answer value

shared.prose: The host retains the first fault and its exact received byte context. Earlier accepted verdicts remain available.
shared.title: Rejected validator frame

shared.prose: Zero-based offset of the rejected frame's first byte in received stdout.
shared.title: byte_offset

shared.prose: Base64 encoding of the retained received-byte prefix. Decoding yields those exact bytes.
shared.title: context_b64

shared.prose: True when frame_bytes exceeds retained_bytes.
shared.title: context_truncated

shared.prose: Length of that frame in bytes, excluding its LF separator.
shared.title: frame_bytes

shared.prose: Receiver category utf8, json or structure for the first rejected frame.
shared.title: kind

shared.prose: Human-readable reason the frame failed structural admission.
shared.title: message

shared.prose: runner_host, identifying the rejecting receiver.
shared.title: origin

shared.prose: Number of prefix bytes retained, capped at 256.
shared.title: retained_bytes

shared.prose: The host exposes text only after acquiring a complete or truncated publication with a bounded length and terminating NUL.
shared.title: Worker diagnostic

shared.prose: Retained diagnostic-byte length excluding its terminating NUL, at most <!-- span limits.worker_diagnostic.value_unit -->4,095 bytes<!-- /span --> when validation permits text extraction.
shared.title: length

facts.unknown: The numeric value remains in the report. Known-branch assessments require their own recognized code and publication conditions.

shared.prose: Raw diagnostic publication word: 0 absent, 1 complete, 2 truncated, 3 incomplete; other values remain numeric.
shared.title: state

shared.prose: Host interpretation: absent, incomplete, unknown, complete, truncated or invalid. Invalid identifies an eligible publication whose length or terminator failed validation.
shared.title: status

shared.prose: Diagnostic bytes decoded as UTF-8 with replacement for invalid sequences. The <!-- span limits.worker_diagnostic.value_unit -->4,095 bytes<!-- /span --> bound applies before replacement decoding. The diagnostic status carries whether the worker truncated its buffer.
shared.title: text

shared.prose: The host resolves this account once from the worker's acquired output and submitted plan. Run questions and per-step questions keep their individual support and conflicts.
shared.title: Canonical worker disposition

shared.prose: Conflicting observations referenced by conflicting claims; indices are zero-based within this array.
shared.title: issues

shared.prose: Fixed set of run-level lifecycle claims.
shared.title: questions

context.where: final worker output and plan join

facts.free.condition: Resolve each question from the owning worker's acquired output, unique slot identities and submitted plan. A not_reached or unpublished conclusion requires terminal collection where specified below.
facts.free.effect: Publish the canonical account once and copy its boundary/result claims into per-attempt lifecycle projections. Retain conflicts as issues rather than selecting one conflicting observation.
facts.where: final worker output and plan join

shared.prose:
An exit code or signal is supported after a successful reap. Both representations
produce a D1 conflict. A completed supported slot establishes publication and
can establish entry. Recognized progress at or after an attempt's entry also
establishes entry. A final earlier progress position establishes `not_reached`
only after confirmed reaping and with an incomplete slot; beside a completed
slot it produces D5. Returned-or-later terminal progress beside an incomplete
supported slot produces D5 for result publication. Live collection leaves
missing results unresolved. An unsupported attempt has inapplicable result
publication and an `unsupported` lifecycle summary.
shared.title: Resolving lifecycle claims

shared.prose: Plan-ordered lifecycle claims for each requested step, joined only to uniquely identified worker slots.
shared.title: steps

shared.prose: A completed worker exec slot separates collection, cleanup requests and the owned leader reap. Collection facts are frozen before termination requests.
shared.title: Spawned-command observation

shared.prose: Requests to terminate the spawned process group and any leader fallback.
shared.title: cleanup

shared.prose: Leader-exit and pipe observations up to the collection stop.
shared.title: collection

shared.prose: Final bounded wait account for the owned leader after collection and cleanup.
shared.title: reap

shared.prose: Cleanup requests follow the frozen collection observation and preserve their native returns.
shared.title: Exec cleanup

shared.prose: SIGKILL request to negative leader PID for the owned process group, when cleanup is requested.
shared.title: group_request

shared.prose: SIGKILL request to the positive leader PID after a failed group request with errno other than ESRCH.
shared.title: leader_fallback

shared.prose: not_requested after leader_exit_and_eof; ownership_unconfirmed when waitid failed; requested when an eligible process-group cleanup was attempted.
shared.title: state

shared.prose: The collector can observe leader exit and pipe EOF independently; descendants may keep a stream open after the leader exits.
shared.title: Exec collection

shared.prose: Local numeric clock-fault observation when collection stopped for failed/backward time.
shared.title: clock_fault

shared.prose: child or plan when the selected collection deadline expires; absent on other stop branches. The child allowance and remaining per-worker active-plan allowance are defined by the exec operation.
shared.title: deadline_kind

shared.prose: Whether waitid observed the owned leader's exit during collection.
shared.title: leader_exit_observed

shared.prose: Native poll failure which stopped stream observation; recovered EINTR is excluded.
shared.title: poll_errno

shared.prose: EOF or native read/poll failure retained for stderr.
shared.title: stderr

shared.prose: EOF or native read/poll failure retained for stdout.
shared.title: stdout

shared.prose: leader_exit_and_eof, deadline, observation_error or clock_fault, recording the branch that stopped collection.
shared.title: stop_reason

shared.prose: Native waitid failure which stopped leader observation; recovered EINTR is excluded.
shared.title: waitid_errno

shared.prose: Final wait facts concern the spawned leader owned by the worker. After collection ends, the production reap allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_reap_grace.value_unit -->1,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> of continuous time. Earlier ownership or group-request failures retain their branch priority; a recorded request and an observed reap remain separate.
shared.title: Exec leader reap

shared.prose: Local numeric clock fault encountered by the reap wait, when observed.
shared.title: clock_fault

shared.prose: Last native waitpid result, with status only when the owned leader PID returned.
shared.title: last_wait

shared.prose: reaped, wait_error, ownership_unconfirmed, group_request_failed, clock_fault or deadline; branch priority preserves earlier ownership/group-request failures.
shared.title: stop_reason

shared.prose: This is the worker's native kill call for a spawned command, scoped to the target named here.
shared.title: Exec signal request

shared.prose: Positive native errno captured for rc -1; absent after success.
shared.title: errno

shared.prose: Native kill return, zero or -1.

shared.prose:
The host binds each validator collection to its phase and retains accepted records through later I/O, association or cleanup failure.

For N submitted queries, the collector assigns a record allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_records_per_query.value -->2<!-- /span --> and a stdout retention allowance of max(1, N) multiplied by <!-- span limits.validator_reply_bytes_per_query.value_unit -->16,384 bytes<!-- /span -->. The allowances are sized before writing the query batch. On byte overflow the host counts all bytes received, keeps the bounded prefix through its last complete LF frame, closes collection and reports byte_limit. Decoding retains complete accepted records before the first refused frame or record-count excess.

shared.prose:
A source may combine a parameter with a literal suffix:

```scheme
(version 1)
(deny default)
(allow file-read* (literal (string-append (param "ROOT") "/hosts")))
```

`"params":{"ROOT":"/etc"}` supplies the value used by this expression. An unused `OPTIONAL` parameter and a referenced but missing `ROOT` exercise different compiler paths. Inspect the native compile record for the latter's outcome.
shared.title: Parameter expressions

facts.free.effect: Sort parameter keys, transport their complete strings, create native parameters only for a nonempty map, and pass each key and value through sandbox_set_param before compiling the selected source. Report setup or compile failure at the observed native stage.

Spawn with target as argv[0], an empty environment, /dev/null stdin, captured stdout/stderr, close-on-exec descriptor policy and a new process group.

shared.prose: A successful spawn supplies a child PID even if the child later exits nonzero. The child collection, termination request and owned reap remain separate observations. The production per-child collection allowance is <!-- span limits.exec_child_wait.value_unit -->10,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> after successful spawn, capped by the remaining per-worker active-plan allowance of <!-- span limits.exec_attempt_budget.value_unit -->115,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The active-plan clock starts before worker setup, includes setup and intervening work, and excludes acknowledged release waits and accepted actor parked-activation waits. Both allowances use continuous time, including system sleep. Exhausted allowance can refuse a later spawn or stop collection; clock faults retain their own boundary. Blocking native calls can outlast the allowance.
shared.title: Exec setup and child inputs

facts.free.effect: Dispatch only the admitted kind/action pair, record the operation's native observations and publish its slot after the attempt. Preserve operation-specific success meaning alongside the aggregate result.
Refuse exec probes in every actor participating in an extension operation, including an actor named only as a transfer recipient. Other actors may declare exec probes.

shared.prose: The worker operation implementations and exec setup branches were read. Fresh-file effects, closed-descriptor inheritance, syscall buffers and cleanup behavior still need their existing control runs attached to the release evidence. The legacy open operations intentionally retain their open-boundary aggregate meaning.
shared.title: Operation controls to attach

shared.prose:
The worker runs the selected operation after policy application in an apply worker, or after the unapplied actor's setup:

| Kind / action | Native operation and operation-specific consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `file / open_read` | `open(O_RDONLY)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte read and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; read and close results are discarded. |
| `file / open_write` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_TRUNC)`; on an accepted descriptor, request a one-byte `x` write and close. Aggregate success is the successful open; write and close results are discarded. |
| `file / create` | `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CREAT, 0600)` then close. Creation mode is subject to umask. An existing file is opened without truncation or exclusive creation. |
| `file / read_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_RDONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)`, `fstat`, one read bounded by <!-- span limits.fresh_read_bytes.value_unit -->64 bytes<!-- /span -->, then close. Record each boundary and read bytes; aggregate failure selects stat, read or close failure after a successful open. |
| `file / write_fresh` | Fresh `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC)` of an existing target, opened `fstat`, `ftruncate(0)`, truncated `fstat`, one-byte `x` write after successful truncation, written `fstat`, then close. Preserve the first failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / create_fresh` | `lstat` before a fresh exclusive `open(O_WRONLY \| O_CLOEXEC \| O_CREAT \| O_EXCL, 0600)`, opened `fstat`, one-byte `x` write, written `fstat`, then close. Pre-open `lstat` is an independent observation. Preserve the first operation failure in the aggregate. |
| `file / unlink` | `unlink(target)` and its return/errno. |
| `file / access` | `access(target, R_OK)` and its return/errno. This is an access-check observation. |
| `mach / lookup` | Obtain the task bootstrap port and call `bootstrap_look_up` for the supplied name; release the returned service port on success. |
| `sysctl / read` | One `sysctlbyname` call with a <!-- span limits.sysctl_read_bytes.value_unit -->4,096 bytes<!-- /span --> buffer acquired after application. Report the call's result and errno; discard value bytes and the returned length. |
| `exec / spawn` | Prepare per-attempt child resources, call `posix_spawn` for the absolute target with the requested argv, then collect child and cleanup observations. |

A short fresh write records its native count and fails the aggregate while retaining zero native errno when the write returned a short nonnegative count. A fresh file descriptor belongs to that attempt and is closed before its result is published.
shared.title: Native operations

shared.prose: Operation target, bounded by <!-- span limits.attempt_target.value_unit -->511 UTF-8 bytes<!-- /span --> and NUL-free. Exec requires an absolute path. Other admitted targets retain their supplied native-operation meaning.

shared.prose:
| Category | Current code examples and condition |
| --- | --- |
| JSON and required values | `invalid_json`, `invalid_value`, `missing_field`, `missing_value`, `type_mismatch`; decoder structure or required-value failure. |
| Public identity and closed objects | `unsupported_contract`; assertion differs or expected identity is unbound. `unknown_field`; undeclared object key. |
| Plan form and identifiers | `exclusive_plan_forms`, `actors_require_phases`, `empty_phases`, `empty_actors`, `empty_actor_id`, `empty_phase_id`, `empty_step_id`, `duplicate_actor_id`, `duplicate_phase_id`, `duplicate_step_id`, `actor_without_phases`. |
| Policy and query | `unresolved_augments`, `unsupported_policy_format`, `missing_policy_source`, `invalid_capture_nonce`, `empty_operation`, `unknown_filter_kind`, `missing_filter_value`. |
| Attempt and applicability | `unsupported_attempt`, `relative_exec_target`, `inapplicable_field`. Inapplicability includes non-exec args, ordinary actor-only fields, disabled-capture nonce and extraneous extension operands. |
| Actor and equipment | `unsupported_sandbox_mode`, `unsupported_equipment`, `unknown_actor`, `empty_entitlement`, `duplicate_entitlement`, `invalid_termination_dependency`, `empty_equipment_overrides`, `relative_equipment_path`. |

shared.prose:
| Value | Host commitment |
| --- | --- |
| `finished` | Execution and required collection completed under the classifier's conditions; each attempt retains its own result. |
| `bad_request` | Reached decoding/admission refused the specimen before worker or validator execution. |
| `bad_policy` | The host could not identify the ordinary source under its structural policy check. |
| `worker_spawn_failed` | The driver could not spawn the worker. |
| `runner_timeout` | Host sentinel or policy-transfer deadline expired, subject to higher-precedence published worker failures. |
| `runner_failed` | Worker preparation/application/publication, host apparatus or supervision failed, or required observations are unusable. |
| `validator_spawn_failed` | Worker classification succeeded and validator spawn failed. |
| `validator_no_reply` | Worker classification succeeded and validator query delivery or verdict reading failed. |
| `validator_decode_failure` | Worker classification succeeded and validator parsing or typed decoding failed. |
| `validator_unavailable` | Required collection was not invoked, its budget/clock failed, or validator supervision/association was unusable. |
| `runner_reporting_failed` | The host failed to validate or encode its assembled report and entered reporting fallback. |

The ordinary worker floor and fixture-delay caps have controls calling the production planning helper and argument parser. The host floors the proposed allowance at <!-- span limits.validator_io_override_floor.value_unit -->50 milliseconds<!-- /span -->; omission uses <!-- span limits.validator_io_wait.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. The remaining aggregate collection allowance can reduce the effective timeout below that floor.

Both schedulers clamp it to a minimum of <!-- span limits.validator_collection_override_floor.value_unit -->1 millisecond<!-- /span --> and their configured maximum: <!-- span limits.phase_collection_wait.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> for the ordinary form and <!-- span limits.actor_collection_allowance.value_unit -->30,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> for actors. Omission uses that maximum.

shared.prose: Nonnegative zero-based slot in each worker's own plan. After that attempt returns and its result payload is written, the worker raises SIGKILL before publishing completion. Negative values are omitted. The worker argument parser requires an index below <!-- span limits.probe_steps.value_unit -->256 items<!-- /span -->; an index beyond the worker's actual plan has no reached action to trigger it.
shared.title: worker_kill_before_publish_slot

shared.prose: Positive fixture delay in milliseconds after all declared visits and actions, before terminal publication. The host forwards positive values; the worker argument parser accepts through <!-- span limits.worker_fixture_delay.value_unit -->60,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. A larger forwarded value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted by the host.
shared.title: worker_post_apply_hang_ms

shared.prose: Positive fixture signal requested after completed actions and before terminal publication, including an unapplied actor's visits. The host forwards positive values; the worker accepts signal numbers through 31. A larger value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted. A signal request can return without termination; final process observations decide the ending.
shared.title: worker_post_apply_kill_signal

shared.prose: Positive fixture delay in milliseconds after compilation and optional capture, before an apply worker's readiness byte and policy application. The host forwards positive values; the worker argument parser accepts through <!-- span limits.worker_fixture_delay.value_unit -->60,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. A larger value causes worker argument refusal after launch. Zero and negative values are omitted. The unapplied actor branch bypasses this compile/readiness path.
shared.title: worker_pre_ready_hang_ms

shared.prose: Ordinary worker sentinel budget override in milliseconds. The host floors the supplied allowance at <!-- span limits.worker_timeout_override_floor.value_unit -->50 milliseconds<!-- /span -->; omission uses <!-- span limits.worker_sentinel_wait.value_unit -->120,000 milliseconds<!-- /span -->. Actor scheduling uses its fixed <!-- span limits.actor_execution_allowance.value_unit -->120,000 milliseconds<!-- /span --> allowance even when this field is supplied.

shared.prose: The decoder follows its object and branch order. A capacity failure can precede a semantic failure in a successfully decoded object. Admission accepts or refuses the complete plan; it preserves declared action counts. Empty ordinary plans still compile and apply the policy.

{"contract":"<reported-contract>","specimen_id":"apply-only","policy":{"format":"sbpl","sbpl_source":"(version 1) (allow default)"},"probe_plan":[]}
